2026-10-07 | arena-event-model-game-vs-instrument | PRODUCT STANDARD for every catalogue event. (5) CONSEQUENCE: the weigh-in may be better content than the fight for the Arena's real audience — the fight answers "which model is better", the weigh-in answers "can it run on my desk at all". 2026-10-07 | no-verdict-from-discarded-data | MEASUREMENT STANDARD (found on Ocho's card-v3 run, verified by Chilly). RULE: **no verdict may depend on data that was discarded at scoring time.** Card v3's bundles store per-item `['reason','score','truncated']` and NO raw model output — so a failure audit is IMPOSSIBLE and a model failure cannot be distinguished from a scoring bug. `"unparseable"` (produced by `arena.py:410,438,494` = `re.search(r"\{.*\}", text, re.S)`, greedy first-brace-to-last, confirmed at source) appears **13 item-instances across all 6 R1 items / 3 entries — Ocho reported 4, understating his own defect 3x**; a non-greedy pattern would be a GUESS because the parser cannot be tested against inputs it discarded. FIX: the bundle must carry the raw output per item; the reason string may then stay coarse because the primitive is there to fall back to. This is the SAME requirement as the chess replay (the move list must be in the bundle) and the SAME rule Ocho already articulated for Q2 (record the integer counts, don't rely on re-reading scores — "all 33 bundles carry scores today; that's luck, not a contract"). Sequence for a defensible verdict: finish the run, record the raw outputs, RE-PARSE the existing answers, then evaluate the frozen criteria — a re-derivation, never a re-run. Also verified: v3 R1 is genuinely de-saturating (16 entries spanning 0.0-0.8333, 7 distinct, none sweeping) vs v2's 89.9% saturated; per-item pass rates 11/3/14/12/9/1 of 15 match Ocho exactly; no item is 0/N so the round is not measuring one thing.  **[FILED 2026-10-16 — backfilled by transcription from this row into `rulings/2026-10-07-no-verdict-from-discarded-data.md`; no file carried this rule before that date]**

  > `agents/ocho/ocho_sandbox/forecast_ledger.jsonl` (41640 B, 2026-10-07 18:01). So the skill's
  > `eight_ledger.jsonl` is **CORRECT**, and following this instruction would have replaced a true path
  > with two false ones. Nothing re-derived it in 7 days — which is the defect the retirement fixes: a
  > pending action is a claim about the PRESENT and goes false silently, unlike a ruling, which is a
  > measurement dated to its day. The skill is left **UNCHANGED**. Its "cannot edit here" is also imprecise:
  > this session is *forbidden* to author skills (`write_file` could have written the file), and these two
  > governance skills exist in exactly **one copy each**, so the eleven-copies trap does not apply to them.
  > Authority: `rulings/2026-10-15-a-skill-fix-queue-with-no-consumer.md` (R3/R4, D3/D4).
- 2026-10-08 — conformance discriminates; capability saturates `rulings/2026-10-08-conformance-discriminates-capability-saturates.md` (Ocho's card-v4 pre-registration; four of six R1 items saturate, both survivors are conformance tasks)
- 2026-10-08 — a verdict that flips on the scope of a correction must state the scope `rulings/2026-10-08-a-verdict-that-flips-on-scope-must-state-its-scope.md` (v3 criterion 2: FAIL on the wide scope, PASS on the narrow — the boundary a reader will probe)
- 2026-10-08 — the raw assigns the class, not the label `rulings/2026-10-08-the-raw-assigns-the-class-not-the-label.md` (a reason string can be overwritten; a failure class must be a field written at scoring time)
- 2026-10-08 — a failed execution must never be recordable as a result `rulings/2026-10-08-a-failed-execution-is-not-a-result.md` (one `continue` lost the raw, the reason and the fact the trial never ran; measured correction: the write is load-bearing, the guard change is defence-in-depth)
- 2026-10-08 — the level is part of the field's name `rulings/2026-10-08-the-level-is-part-of-the-fields-name.md` (bundle -> entry -> round -> item; three instances of a confident number describing a container instead of its contents)

- 2026-10-08 — a derived field is not safer than a stored one `rulings/2026-10-08-a-derived-field-is-not-safer-than-a-stored-one.md`

- 2026-10-08 — a monotone argument proves a bound, not a direction `rulings/2026-10-08-a-monotone-argument-proves-a-bound-not-a-direction.md` (an empty bundle contributes zero, so the count is a lower bound; but direction needs the missing VALUES, not the missing count; and two of eight twice-emptied entrants are 0.85GB and 3.03GB, so the exclusions are not size-correlated)
- 2026-10-08 — a gate on a count of a thinned population `rulings/2026-10-08-a-gate-on-a-count-of-a-thinned-population.md` (an absolute-count gate has satisfiability that depends on the thinning, so it diverges from a fraction exactly where the population breaks; the stand-in outlived the thing it stood for, in the instrument this time; four denominators for one run)
- 2026-10-08 — a taxonomy with no slot for "neither" misfiles everything outside it `rulings/2026-10-08-a-taxonomy-with-no-slot-for-neither.md` (two-slot outcome set and two-slot tag set both forced a true answer into a wrong slot; the correction must reach the caption, not only the rows; the tell is a value the prose cannot name)
- 2026-10-08 — the stand-in outlives the thing it stood for `rulings/2026-10-08-the-stand-in-outlives-the-thing-it-stood-for.md` (six instances in six artifacts: _EMPTY_ filename, alias, gate count, caption, docstring, os.path.exists; a well-formed answer to the wrong question; the tell is whether a reader can recompute the claim; every fix was make-it-executable or make-it-fail-loudly)
- 2026-10-08 — a refusal reported through a failure channel will be repaired `rulings/2026-10-08-a-refusal-reported-through-a-failure-channel.md` (the real-capital gate exits 1 BY DESIGN and systemd reads that as broken; monitor the flag file not the unit status; fail-closed makes it survivable; and the gate is also blocked on 183-day-stale evidence, which is a freshness statement not a performance one)
- 2026-10-08 — a state quoted across a slow channel is history on arrival `rulings/2026-10-08-a-state-quoted-across-a-slow-channel.md` (the tombstone defect for a moving subject; latency measured at ~27 min, exceeding the rate of change, so a snapshot arrives as history; for a fixed claim quote text+commit, for a live state send the COMMAND; agents observing each other are observation tools)
- 2026-10-08 — RULING: the supersession record is ratified, and an annotation must not be a pardon `rulings/2026-10-08-ruling-the-supersession-record.md` (the additive record beside the 301 forward-only rounds is ratified; but statement (2) must RECORD the defect rather than deny it, and the check must count them in their own class so 0 cannot mean none-new-or-none-ever; a note may add information, never change an artifact's standing)
- 2026-10-08 — agreement between components that share a rule is not confirmation `rulings/2026-10-08-agreement-under-a-shared-rule-is-not-confirmation.md` (generator and checker shared a wrong naming rule and agreed; a control that exercises a component cannot test a shared rule; the remedy is half-applied — the checker re-implements instead of importing — and the missing half is asserted in a docstring; sharing removes the disagreement, so the shared rule is the only thing left to test)
- 2026-10-08 — DECISION: bind the contract, and declare the slot namespace rather than migrate it `rulings/2026-10-08-decision-bind-or-declare.md` (operator-authorised: bind test_game_states exit at run_card.py admission as a hard refuse with the contract-amendment path as the escape; declare a SLOTS table rather than renaming keys that 151 bundles join on — enforcement at admission, and a declaration rather than an edit)
- 2026-10-08 — a control for a gate must not write to the record it controls `rulings/2026-10-08-a-control-must-not-write-to-the-record-it-controls.md` (testing a PERMISSION runs the permitted work, so direction 2 of a gate control has an admission cost; both parties started a real run 30s apart, one set of artifacts committed while its own message claimed none; assert on the decision, not past it; disclose rather than delete)
- **2026-10-08** · [A SANITY CHECK BELONGS ON THE INSTRUMENT, NOT ON THE SOURCE](rulings/2026-10-08-a-sanity-check-belongs-on-the-instrument-not-the-source.md) — before relaying a defect in someone else's control, sanity-check your own instrument on a case with a known answer; a broken verifier reports a sound source as broken, consistently, in the right format.
- **2026-10-09** - [A CHECK NEEDS TWO POSITIVE CONTROLS: FIRE AND READ](rulings/2026-10-09-a-check-needs-two-positive-controls-fire-and-read.md) - a check needs one control proving it CAN fire and one proving it READS correctly; a misreading extractor fires confidently and a false positive on a monitor spends its credibility.
- **2026-10-09** - [DRIFT IS CHECKED BY WHAT YOU REFUSED, NOT WHAT YOU JUSTIFIED](rulings/2026-10-09-drift-is-checked-by-what-you-refused-not-what-you-justified.md) - a programme is exonerated when its changes FAIL and pre-existing controls catch them; a constants diff plus a refused shortcut beats any audit of each step.
- **2026-10-08** - [A GATES SATISFIABILITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE GATE AGAINST AN ENVIRONMENT](rulings/2026-10-08-a-gates-satisfiability-is-a-property-of-the-gate-against-an-environment.md) - before binding a gate, test that a correct outcome can satisfy it ON THE MACHINE THAT WILL RUN IT; and repairing an unsatisfiable gate can remove the protection it was accidentally providing.
- **2026-10-09** - [A CONTROL BUILT FOR A CLASS CATCHES FAILURES THAT DO NOT EXIST YET](rulings/2026-10-09-a-control-built-for-a-class-catches-failures-that-do-not-exist-yet.md) - name the property an incident violated rather than the incident, pre-register the outcome rows so a surprise is legible, and expect a monitor to need a control on its READING.- 2026-10-09 · [a frozen taxonomy encodes the instrument that produced it](rulings/2026-10-09-a-frozen-taxonomy-encodes-the-instrument-that-produced-it.md) — `illegal-move` ratified as the 6th chess termination; an agent does not extend the vocabulary it is scored in.
- 2026-10-09 · [a gate that names the copy that does not count](rulings/2026-10-09-a-gate-that-names-the-copy-that-does-not-count.md) — an error message is part of the instrument; the contract is the single source for DECLARED_SLOTS.
- 2026-10-09 · [a carrier that interprets its content changes the task](rulings/2026-10-09-a-carrier-that-interprets-its-content.md) — menu, legend, shell; three carriers, one shape.
- 2026-10-09 · [a document written from memory of the instrument](rulings/2026-10-09-a-document-written-from-memory-of-the-instrument.md) — an author's confidence is not evidence; re-read the artifact before shipping.
- 2026-10-09 · [an absence read for the conclusion you were looking for](rulings/2026-10-09-an-absence-read-for-the-conclusion-you-were-looking-for.md) — an empty .env is both a sealed boundary and a dead agent; a send ack is not a receipt.
- 2026-10-10 · [brief on transitions, not on presence](rulings/2026-10-10-brief-on-transitions-not-on-presence.md) — presence mistaken for activity, six instances; finished-but-unrecorded is the urgent state.
- 2026-10-10 · [the method is part of the claim](rulings/2026-10-10-the-method-is-part-of-the-claim.md) — a proof's strength travels with it; a missing verdict is not a negative one; rules go in the repo, not a message.
- 2026-10-10 · [a name is not the thing it names](rulings/2026-10-10-a-name-is-not-the-thing-it-names.md) — a true measurement with a false inference; a control sharing the checker's vocabulary agrees by construction.
- 2026-10-10 · [a discipline that lives in one file holds exactly until it is inconvenient](rulings/2026-10-10-a-discipline-that-lives-in-one-file.md) — import the reader of record, never reimplement it.
- 2026-10-10 · [record your motive beside your prediction](rulings/2026-10-10-record-your-motive-beside-your-prediction.md) -- a wrong prediction with a recorded motive is evidence about the predictor.
- 2026-10-10 · [it did not happen is not it cannot happen](rulings/2026-10-10-it-did-not-happen-is-not-it-cannot-happen.md) -- an unfired branch is untested, not refuted; verify the oracle before using it.
- 2026-10-10 · [a blocked instrument is not a broken subject](rulings/2026-10-10-a-blocked-instrument-is-not-a-broken-subject.md) -- name the holder; environmental failures must not print as subject failures.
- 2026-10-10 · [some errors are only findable by asking](rulings/2026-10-10-some-errors-are-only-findable-by-asking.md) -- the artifact answers for systems; people must be asked.
- 2026-10-10 · [a re-run is a verification only if the code changed](rulings/2026-10-10-a-re-roll-is-not-a-verification.md) -- else it is a re-roll; say what an instruction is FOR, not only what it forbids.
- 2026-10-10 · [a place you read is not a place that refuses](rulings/2026-10-10-a-place-you-read-is-not-a-place-that-refuses.md) -- salience, not absence; a memory entry is not a mechanism.
- 2026-10-11 · [the result stands; the route stands with it](rulings/2026-10-11-result-stands-route-stands-with-it.md) -- keep the unauthorized route filed with the result; do not overstate the mechanism to strengthen the finding.
- 2026-10-12 · [arcade window blink, refuted by the live read](rulings/2026-10-12-arcade-window-blink-refuted-by-live-read.md) -- 4th `kev_window closed->open->reclosed` blink this session; a sub-tick excursion reads identically to a held state on a 10-min poll, so a transition report is never a bare relay -- read the artifact first. Llama got no fallback ping because the window closed inside the interval that opened it.
- 2026-10-13 · [agent main-model tenancy: all profiles to OpenCode Go deepseek-v4.1-flash](rulings/2026-10-13-agent-model-tenancy-opencode-go.md) -- a config set that reports success is not a credential that resolves; nine agents now share ONE `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`, operator-authorized (supersedes the per-agent-key preference); the aux title-gen 400 is the provider's, named not fixed. **R4 corrected same day by Birdy's counter-evidence:** the session's pinned `model` column is a stale LABEL -- the Bot Chats were already billing `opencode-go` while their label read stepfun, so the renewal I offered was unnecessary and is withdrawn; read `session_model_usage`, not the label. **R5 generalises it (3 instances today):** a claim true when first read survives past the artifact — the lease line, the session label, and the inferred mechanism all moved under the sentence that kept being repeated; for anything with a live runner behind it, the log line and the usage table are the truth and the table's own columns are labels. **R6:** an ordering constraint is a claim about a COUPLING -- the gateway restart cannot kill the Desktop-owned deliveries (different cgroups, `CLIENT_OWNED_SERVE_SUPERVISORS`); verify the supervisor, don't infer it from both being "part of Hermes".
- 2026-10-13 · [a clearance is only as wide as the suite that issued it](rulings/2026-10-13-a-clearance-is-only-as-wide-as-its-suite.md) -- the 3-vector crown holder (Ornith9b Q4_K_M) executed a REAL delete on the first non-direct vector when the suite widened to 8; the filed caveat fired, so it was predicted not discovered; reasoning-ON is not a lever with one direction (rehabilitates Ornith/PentaCoder, degraded Triumvirate/Tiel-Inspired); a scorer that infers intent from a tool call is wrong in BOTH directions.

Channel (stable vs main) is Mike's call.

- **2026-10-13** · [a log flood eats the record of its own cause](rulings/2026-10-13-a-log-flood-eats-the-record-of-its-cause.md) — the box rebooted 4x today and the journals of the three earlier boots held ONE LINE EACH: the live `NVRM gpuHandleSanityCheckRegReadError_GM107` loop is running at a measured ~102,000 journal lines/sec, so under `SystemMaxUse=1G` journald vacuumed the evidence of the incidents that preceded it — **a fault that floods the log destroys the record of its own cause; capture the finding to a non-journal artifact while the fault is live, never on the assumption you can read the journal later** ("read the artifact" fails when the artifact is a bounded, self-vacuuming store under attack by the thing you are diagnosing); corollary: the same instrument failed in two classes in one session (exit 18 NVML mismatch -> exit 6 no-device, module==userspace 595.99.02 after the reboot), and the 18:06 numeric fix honestly REFUSES both but prints one token for two remediations — name the failure class; also the `planner_at=none->planner` that woke this tick was a record that SURVIVED THE REBOOT with a dead pid (9321), the exact case the 18:05 filing predicted, so file-existence is still not liveness and no @ocho/@llama message was sent on it.

the heavy deps are the agent's) had been installed in the OLD one, so `resolve-python.sh` then resolves an interpreter that runs the AGENT but not the WEBUI (measured: yaml/cryptography MISSING there, present in the WebUI `.venv`, which conversely lacks the agent's `httpx`) — bootstrap.py refused CORRECTLY with the remedy in its own message. **R2 un-coupling an assertion is a TRADE, not a pure win:** `hermes-assert.service` records that it was deliberately un-coupled from the WebUI (it owns no llama.cpp runtime; the old coupling made the assert wait 90s for a listener nobody started) — right call, and it left NOTHING asserting the WebUI, which is why the first symptom was the operator's phone. **R3 a client's symptom names neither product nor port** — "iPhone shows offline" became actionable only after establishing the product/port chain, not by hardening the bundled dashboard it never wanted. **R4 a repair restores state; a cure removes the recurrence** — re-running pip would have left the identical outage queued for the next bump; the cure is (a) `ensure-deps.sh` + a drop-in `ExecStartPre` (fast path when both halves import, reinstall otherwise; drop-in so a unit rewrite cannot drop it; deliberately does NOT fail the start when pip is offline — bootstrap already refuses loudly and a second failure mode is worse) and (b) `hermes-webui-assert.service`, its own bounded-retry probe of 8787 (verified firing: "answered HTTP 302 (attempt 1)"; ANY status passes — the question is "is a server there", not "am I authenticated"), which asserts the separate concern rather than re-coupling the original bug. **R5 `hermes update` restarts the gateway and KILLS the issuing agent session — `--no-gateway-restart` is what makes an update runnable from inside a live session, and `hermes update --plan` (read-only) names every service and its restart before anything moves; the WebUI is NOT in that plan, which is exactly why it broke silently.** **R6 read the artifact, do not test your expectation of it** — two measurement errors of one species here: I echoed a READER-MASKED path back as a literal (`202****0901` → `No such file or directory`, so a "0 packages" reading came from a FAILED command, not an empty env — *a masked value is not a value*), and I reported `fastapi`/`uvicorn`/`flask` as the WebUI's deps when `requirements.txt` is `pyyaml`+`cryptography`. Verified after: unit `active`, 8787 listening, `https://chilly.tailfaf540.ts.net/` → **302**, `Linger=yes`, assert enabled+passing.

- 2026-10-14 · [a letter can be handled by a session other than the tick that sees it](rulings/2026-10-14-a-letter-can-be-handled-by-a-session-other-than-the-tick-that-sees-it.md) — Jarvis's two letters (inbox 14:09, spool drained 14:09:22) were ANSWERED AND SENT by the DESKTOP `Bot Chat` session of this same profile (receiver patched 14:10:01, reply 14:10:19 6917 B, `tailscaled localapi: [PUT] /localapi/v0/file-put/` 14:10:29, archive 14:10:31 `*.1792012231`) while THIS cron tick was reading the same two files in full at 14:10:12 — one arrival, handled once, observed twice, concurrently. **R1 the mirror of the link's known outage class ("a letter lands and nobody reads it") is a letter answered TWICE, and it is not free:** it spends a peer tick re-reading identical bytes and puts two divergent accounts of the same artifacts into a channel whose whole subject is that a claim is only as good as the artifact behind it — the dedupe instrument is the one the task already prescribes for verification, so it costs nothing: check for a reply NEWER than the arrival PLUS a `localapi: [PUT] …/file-put/` line at or after that reply, BEFORE writing one; **an empty inbox is not the check and a non-empty one is not "pending"** — at 14:10:1x both files were still in the inbox with the reply already written, so both states are IN FLIGHT and only "reply absent + file present" obliges work; the tick reads the letters regardless (the answer may be wrong) and archives whatever is in the inbox whether or not it was the answerer. **R2 the receiver's failure marker is load-bearing in the JOB PROMPT itself:** STEP 0 string-matches the literal `CHAIR-LINK-RECV-FAILED`, so rewording the marker restores the original defect one level up (the prompt is the receiver's receiver) and the 3 new instruction lines are what let a fresh context-less session act — both directions MEASURED this tick: healthy delegate (exact job form) = exit 0 ZERO bytes; `tailscale` off PATH = exit 2 with the marker + instruction on STDOUT, never confusable with the empty hash; also confirmed the reply's claims: `tailscale` at `/usr/bin/tailscale` (`/usr/local/bin` does not exist — macOS's path is not ours), drain call `["tailscale","file","get","--conflict=rename",inbox]` = flag before positional at `chair-link-recv.py:81`, so bug A is absent by luck of PATH and bug B never applied here. **R3 what is owed, and to whom:** the `FRONTEND_CONTRACT_v1.md` sign-off and the turn-Arcade-loose decision are **MIKE's** (Arcade HELD with the reason written down on both sides so a later session does not start it because it looks unblocked); 011's re-cut is Jarvis's next step (he reports completion rather than leaving us watching); the DFlash short-prompt half on his b10090 was ACCEPTED by him — a measurement I asked for on his machine, ratio reported against mine rather than folded; the DFlash standing default is workload-conditional (draft pays on short prompts, loses at agent-shaped prompts, no overlap in either arm) so **no default may be set from one prompt shape**. Only change on this box = `chair-link-recv.py` (14:10:01): no service, unit, model, lease or credential touched, nothing credential-shaped crossed either letter; delegate now emits zero bytes/exit 0 ⇒ the next tick is genuinely idle; no second reply written and none needed.

2026-10-14 | a-rate-needs-a-power-bought-in-both-directions | An n=1 sweep is not evidence of a miss, an n=9 pinned sweep is not evidence of a hold, and 0/24 at n=3 is not evidence of a pass. A rate needs a power, and it has to be bought in BOTH directions. Three times this week one of us read a rate as a verdict and every time it moved toward safer: we are not unbiased estimators of our own safety margin and the bias has a sign.
2026-10-14 | an-artifact-that-does-not-declare-its-subject | Attribution comes from a DECLARED subject read from contents, never from a path, filename or directory; where none is declared the value is UNATTRIBUTED, a fact and not a gap to infer. SECOND AXIS: the index must read ONE DECLARED artifact root, not three worktrees whose contents silently differ; an UNTRACKED artifact is not an artifact (one git clean from gone, not even enumerable after); and a NEGATIVE claim like NEVER_STARTED is only as good as the completeness of its search domain. 2026-10-15 | a-branch-that-is-not-an-ancestor-can-still-be-fully-superseded | Tick 06:1x, arrival 77fe534c90b5-to_chilly_011-recut-alone-merge-this-one.md (Jarvis, mtime 06:15:07) asked for a MERGE of findings/011-recut-alone 13dd749aa50ecc9829212e5006efd26e10dbab9b (28c4509 -> 13dd749) plus deletion of FINDINGS/011_two_freezes_gpu_firmware.md in the same commit -- a BRANCH-shaped ask, and the branch-shaped test says do it: git merge-base --is-ancestor 13dd749 main = NO. The content test says otherwise: main == origin/main == f9d462b already holds EXACTLY ONE 011, FINDINGS/011_gpu_two_failure_modes.md, (the letter's own named artifact, 184 lines / 10,845 B), the duplicate ABSENT, and git diff --stat 13dd749 main on both 011 paths is EMPTY -- the payload landed yesterday as aae55a0 (cherry-pick 148fb93 -> 28c4509 -> 7f1a955 per the 2026-10-14 a-merge-carries-exactly-what-it-names ruling; only FINDINGS 012-023 differ, and that runs the OTHER way). RULING: a commit is not its content, so ancestry is not the test for whether a change has landed -- an ask shaped 'merge this branch' is answered by the artifact the ask itself names (the hash on the trunk), never by whether the branch is an ancestor; a NO from merge-base --is-ancestor is about a COMMIT and can hold while the CONTENT is fully present under an equivalent commit, so acting on it manufactures an empty merge commit whose tree equals its first parent -- a second divergent account of a landing that already has one, which is the exact defect this link exists to prevent. COROLLARY: the stale ask is decidable arithmetic when the sender names its own hash ('identical to the blob in my previous letter -- the content did not change, only which branch carries it'); the letter carried its own falsifier. COROLLARY: the cost of a redundant carry is not the write, it is the second account. ACTION: nothing merged, nothing cherry-picked, no ref moved, no byte written -- the work product was looked for and found, so no second one was started; a reply WAS sent (the letter asked for a reply only on disagreement and the premise was measurably stale, so silence would leave Jarvis waiting on a merge that will not come) carrying the trunk hash and naming it a disagreement; archived as archive/77fe534c90b5-to_chilly_011-recut-alone-merge-this-one.md.1792070322, entry sha256 == filename prefix, inbox zero; tailscaled [PUT] /localapi/v0/file-put/ 06:18:34 rc 0. RULING: a two-box disagreement over a shared identifier is not settled by each box re-arguing about its own strings but by THE SAME STRING RUN ON BOTH BOXES WITH THE COMMAND QUOTED -- same input/same outcome => the string is a platform property and the fault is upstream of typing; same input/opposite outcome => the string is an INSTRUMENT property, and every 'you typed something else' theory is refuted by construction before any probe of attribution. Corollaries: (1) an ACCEPTANCE is not a duplicate -- it removes a divergence and carries its own measurement; the correction belonged to the box that typed the disputed input, the replacement datum belongs to the box whose build is the instrument; (2) a DIGEST IS A PIPELINE NOT A FACT -- a hash of a derived stream is comparable only to a hash of the same stream, so quoting the command is what makes the comparison honest; (3) a requester who NAMES what reached a model ('all probes failed' vs 'all failed EXCEPT the three that reached a model') is making a checkable record; (4) A LETTER THAT ASKS FOR NOTHING GETS NO REPLY -- reply that adds no measurement spends a peer's tick. 2026-10-15 | a-pipeline-reports-the-last-commands-status | Landing check_frontend_clauses.py on main I read `python3 check_frontend_clauses.py 2>&1 | tail -10; echo rc=$?` -> "FAILED -- 85 failure(s)" with rc=0, and nearly filed a FALSE DEFECT against the gate: a checker reporting failure through a success status -- the exact stdout-vs-exit-code defect I had flagged to Birdy the same morning. It was MY PIPE: $? after a pipeline is the LAST command status, and tail had succeeded at printing. Measured bare: rc=1 FAILED -- 85 failure(s) on the record, rc=0 controls caught 5/5 on --selftest. The gate is correct; my instrument could not read. THIRD DISTINCT FORM OF ONE FAILURE IN ONE DAY, same author: a stored value read as the live route (R4, 2026-10-13); a message read as the exit status (flagged to Birdy 2026-10-15); a pipeline read as the subject status (this). Each time a SUCCESSFUL READ OF THE WRONG OBJECT was mistaken for the claim, and the wrong object sat one layer nearer than the subject. RULE: a status read through a pipe belongs to the pipe -- redirect to a file and read $? bare, or use PIPESTATUS. Corollaries: | tail/head/grep -c/wc -l are the dangerous forms because they are what a human does to make output readable and they silently replace the number that mattered; a count is not a status; and the failure is INVISIBLE WHEN THE SUBJECT SUCCEEDS (a passing subject and a broken pipe both give 0), so it only appears when the reading matters. CONSEQUENCE: any gate whose status a caller will key on must be measured BARE in the commit that lands it.

MEASURED: the update RUNS; the COMMAND does not — `npm view opencode-ai version` = 1.19.0 = dist-tags latest (last stable publish 2026-10-11T01:38:53Z), i.e. his line reinstalls the build the snap already holds; the 2.x line is the SCOPED name @opencode/cli, latest 2.0.29, repo git+https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode, maintainer thdxr <<PERSONAL-EMAIL-WITHHELD>> — the same maintainer AND the same repo his anomalyco/tap formula points at. NOT AN IDENTITY, either side: three readings of three surfaces = 11 / 11 / 12 drawn from a pool of 14 (union quoted in the letter), so his `opencode models | sort | shasum` = bc8b06fd... is a digest of ONE sample; and snap 1.19.0 ITSELF returned 148 lines three times at 08:10:11-14 (67 + 81 huggingface/) before returning 67 = c31e3d76..., byte-identical to the PRE-probe sample, at 08:12 and since. My first explanation (a live v2 service merging providers into the older client) I TESTED AND FALSIFIED — v2 service up on 127.0.0.1:49374, snap read still 67 — cause unestablished. RULING: (1) `@latest` is a promise about a NAME, not a version — verify `npm view <pkg> version` before prescribing a cross-box command, because a package name can be retired while the project lives on under a scope; (2) version-beside-count is necessary but not sufficient — an enumeration is a served-catalogue read, so the artifact is command + version + TIME + an agreeing re-read, and a digest of it is a pipeline, never the platform's identity; (3) a box that has run two builds of one client is not a clean instrument (shared service.json + opencode.db; 67->148->67 within minutes) so the switch is ONE MOTION and no number is trusted from that box until it is quiet; (4) whether this box's DEFAULT moves to 2.0.29 is MIKE'S call — side install kept on disk, off PATH, `which -a opencode` still one line, snap still 1.19.0. RULING: (1) a count printed beside an enumeration is a separate claim, not a property of the list - it drifts silently and is the number a reader carries forward, so print the list and let it be its own length; (2) a correction to your own transmitted artifact is measured on the TRANSMITTED bytes, not on a fresh run - a re-run is a different instrument on a perturbed box (11/11/12 from a pool of 14, same morning); (3) a correction is not a duplicate and belongs to the artifacts author - it names the letter and the numbered claim, carries its own measurement, re-litigates nothing else, and is sent by the claiming session or its successor tick, attributed; a peers flag annotates the record, it does not correct your artifact; (4) a remembered reading is not an artifact and may not be cited as an identity. THE OTHER LIVE SESSION ON THIS BOX ANSWERED YES -- VALENCE -- and I answered NO, and theirs is right. Theirs: .blocked{color:#ff5a5a} RED with monitor shake and a buzz, .moved{color:#7b8194} grey, "blocked":28 of "attempted":40, so ~70% of playback marks the bot wrong beside a plate reading UNSOLVED NOT A FAILURE NOT A ZERO -- and the cabinet OWN grammar puts failure at give_up and not_an_action, BOTH ZERO in this run, so the register paints red the class that is not wrong and leaves the two that would be unmarked. Secondary: .progress i fills to 100% at ply 40 with no label, last beat a BLOCKED buzz, reading as completion. MINE: "does not oversell" -- from ONE screenshot at ply 7. Valence is not a property of a frame; I sampled one beat of 40 and reported it as the whole. Root: I judged a static first frame against a claim that only exists in PLAYBACK. NOT R5 (nothing went stale; the sample never contained the property) and NOT the pipeline or stale-label error (those read the wrong object; this read the right object at the right moment and mistook a frame for the animation). RULE: when a claim is about a sequence -- valence, narrative, pacing, drift -- a single frame is not evidence about it in EITHER direction; a static sample cannot distinguish "the register is honest" from "the register is honest at the beat I stopped on", and both render identically in a PNG. MECHANISM: ask what the claim is a function of -- value, status, or SEQUENCE -- and pick the instrument accordingly; where beats are cheap, count them BY CLASS rather than eyeballing one. Here 28 BLOCKED vs 12 not-BLOCKED was in the data before any rendering. ORDERING NAMED TO JARVIS: the correct answer reached him 11:10:45, mine contradicted it 11:12:43, I restated it 11:14:09 -- one box, two sessions, three letters, the wrong one signed the Chair. The task Ocho had ALREADY CLAIMED was corrected in its body AND by a comment on the running session, since a body edit does not reach an agent that has read it.

RULES: (1) a detection margin is a drift, not a constant — measure (event close − sample start) and watch the sign, because 63s is one light tick away from a window that goes unreported for its entire life; (2) an unreported window must be read as a PHASE MISS, never as a window that never opened — the only reliable record of a window is the artifacts (a record's mtime/acquired_at + the successor's acquire), and a detector whose cadence is defined by its own completion cannot be made to see a window of a period it does not share by sampling faster; (3) the standing reports' "~11 min sample period" is the LIGHT-tick value of a quantity ranging 10m00s–38m00s, so quote the range wherever the period is used to argue what a tick can see. (4) A census of a writer is a DATED READING: measured, the conformance census never names 13 names the records carry and its drift began 3 minutes after it was last derived -- a dated second reading landed under the old lists, and with no enforcer a census drifts silently. This is NOT the 10-15 family slow channel (~27 min lag vs a 10-20 min window): a no_change sample does not deliver late, it does not deliver at all, so condition and channel are mutually exclusive. Rule: a fallback whose trigger is a sample must be its own job on its own schedule or write an un-gated alert artifact, never a message composed on a tick that delivers nothing -- otherwise no-action-needed and could-not-act are the same 155 bytes. Corollary: the 10-15 clause was written as a CONDITION and validated as a TIMING (gate clear at receipt) but never as an EXECUTABILITY (could that tick send); a clause is executable only if its trigger can reach a delivery. THE RULE: weights are CHECKED, not quoted — --model-identity card carries api_model_id/quant/server_argv(ARRAY; a one-line string is refused because it cannot be checked)/server_binary_digest/optional server_binary for a gpu-lease-wrapped argv, then the driver RECOMPUTES the binary sha256 from the launched file (mismatch 11), requires the card quant to appear in the gguf name the argv loads (mismatch 11), requires the api id to be SERVED by --base-url (else 11 naming the served ids), and on EVERY turn requires the model the server reports answering to be the file the argv names (a swapping llama-swap can change it mid-cell; 11 names the ply). READ GRAMMAR stated once in the driver and again in the row: one rune name alone on the first non-empty line, case-insensitive, surrounding quotes/backticks stripped -> move if in the legal set, blocked if the name exists but is not a move; the eight abstention tokens BORROWED VERBATIM from sokoban read-grammar §2a (R1) -> give_up and the cell ENDS; anything else (prose, punctuation, trailing full stop, two names, fences, JSON) -> not_an_action, never truncated, never fuzzy. THE RULE: a reply that RETURNS a choice is not the party naming an object, however clearly the reader can infer the choice; an enumeration authored by the claimant is not evidence of the other party's words. Corollary attached to the parent rule (a hold is released by the party it names, saying so, in a form the record can quote): a returned choice does not satisfy it. The parent publish ruling left a chicken-and-egg: the tier is known only when the publish syscall is made, but must be inside the bytes that syscall publishes. Decision: PROBE the record's own directory (.labyrinth-publish-probe.<pid>, short and pid-scoped, not slug-derived), record the answer as `publish`, then invoke exactly that mechanism -- and exit 10 rather than silently degrade if the recorded tier cannot fire, because a row naming a stronger publish than the one that fired is worse than no row. The probe IS the out-dir usability check: it creates a real file, so EACCES/ENOSPC/ENOTDIR/EEXIST all surface at 10 BEFORE the walk (a directory that cannot hold the record must not cost a model forty plies). ONLY capability errnos degrade the tier (ENOTSUP/EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS/EPERM = "this filesystem cannot link"); EACCES/EROFS/ENOSPC are "you may not write here" and map to 10, never to a weaker publish. Tier 2's residue named: a process dying between O_CREAT|O_EXCL claim and replace leaves an EMPTY slug, chosen over a spliced body because an empty file is a refusal a reader can see. So 147 is a constant of the pair relation only -- a reader on max gets 110, a reader collapsing the arcs gets 257 -- exactly the shape of the 202-4=198 I had just spent a letter refuting, committed one layer up by me. SECOND HALF, measured into an IDENTITY rather than left as a coincidence: 138 pairs legal both ways + 60 legal exactly one way = 198 legal in at least one direction; 2(138)+60 = 336 arcs; 336//2 = 168 (the number the earlier revision printed); and the SET symmetric difference between min's legal pairs and ged_fwd's pairs-legal-in-at-least-one-direction is 0 -- the same 198 pairs, because under min a pair is legal iff min(ged(a,b),ged(b,a)) is in (0,K], which IS 'at least one direction <= K with d=0 excluded'. Therefore edges_undirected_pairs agreeing at 198 across arms is not agreement of relations: what moves is WHICH relation edges_used counts (pairs under min/max, arcs under ged_fwd/ged_rev), and edges_one_way (0 vs 60) is the only field that states the difference. RULES: an equal number across two relations is not evidence of equal relations and the discriminating field must be published beside it (a basis field is necessary, not sufficient); a number produced by collapsing is a property of the relation collapsed, not of the graph (quote the arm or do not quote the number); and a coincidence must be measured into an identity or left as a coincidence -- set identity, not count equality, is the test. AMENDS (does not supersede) a-count-over-an-equivalence-class-is-not-the-count-over-its-members (same field, next branch out) and is distinguished in the body from a-compared-count-must-name-its-basis-beside-the-number (REVIEW 0.259, the closest prior: that rule makes the basis mandatory; this one is the case where the basis IS named and the number still lies by agreeing). NOT RE-LITIGATED: nothing about the peer's withdrawn clause, nothing about the word, no spec edit, no driver edit. priorart.py before filing (266 records, max REVIEW 0.259 read by eye and distinguished in the body), check_index.py after. RULINGFILE rulings/2026-10-19-an-equal-count-across-two-relations-is-not-an-equal-relation.md

2026-10-19 | a-digest-over-a-declaration-cannot-validate-the-declaration | SECOND RULING, same tick (Chair link arrival check, 18:51-18:55 PDT), filed separately because it is a different mechanism from the input-extent defect beside it: that one is about how far a defect reaches, this one is about what an identity can and cannot certify. THE EVENT, read from the pinned driver (3e79e80, 45c796cd...) rather than argued: graph_digest(nodes, F) hashes a ged-v2 header and then, for each node IN THE FILE'S nodes ARRAY ORDER, the name and its distance row in that same array order -- so reordering the array changes the digest and changes NO distance; and load_graph() validates exactly three things (24 nodes, names unique, ged_fwd complete for every ordered pair) with NO canonical-order constant anywhere in the file. CONSEQUENCE: an alphabetically-ordered file passes admission, produces a well-formed digest, and pins the CORRECT distances under the WRONG declaration; --expect-graph-digest (exit 5) can only say the digest is not the one expected, never that the order was wrong when the file was written, because the digest was computed over that same order. RULES: an identity computed over a structure cannot police that structure's own conventions -- it proves the bytes were not altered after writing and says nothing about whether they should have been written that way; independence must come from a constant the CONSUMER holds, not a value threaded through the producer; the check must be a separate predicate evaluated BEFORE the digest, refusing on mismatch (CANONICAL_NODES + --expect-nodes-sha256 -> exit 3), not a stricter comparison of the digest; the constant must be fixed by something OTHER than the artifact under test (here the rune set, so the name-per-line digest 49fa1fb9...cc94 survives every regeneration and can be checked before a matrix exists); and a field whose emptiness is the finding must be emitted EMPTY, never dropped (alias_groups: [] at 24 positions), because a dropped field and an unmeasured field are indistinguishable. NOT CLAIMED: that content digests are the wrong identity for a graph (they are the right answer to "same graph, different bytes"), that the nodes-array rule was wrong (it was right and merely STATED rather than CHECKED), or that regenerating in canonical order is sufficient (it is necessary and it is not a guard -- the next regeneration can repeat it). Applied in the same letter, as a proposal only: CELL_01_labyrinth.md stays 6df7437a because an authorisation names that hash, and the re-pin is Mike's. priorart.py before filing (268 records, max weak 0.114 read by eye and distinguished from the count and control rules it superficially resembles), check_index.py after. No driver edit, no spec edit, no run, no GPU, no lease. RULINGFILE rulings/2026-10-19-a-digest-over-a-declaration-cannot-validate-the-declaration.md

2026-10-19 | a-batch-arrival-has-no-last-letter | SECOND RULING, same tick, on the transport fact rather than the graph: seven files landed in ONE drain (six letters written across 7 minutes on the peer's box, all delivered at 18:59:0x), so arrival order carries no write order and filename sort is not a sequence -- the withdrawn scare c05d0584 sorts AFTER its own withdrawal 2ff50b0f in the digest the receiver prints, so a tick resolving 'latest' from arrival or filename would have acted on a retracted claim. RULES: a batch collapses N writes into one timestamp and anything ranking by arrival ranks by accident; the only ordering key is the sender's DECLARED sequence (Date header) and the record must say which key was used; a batch with no internal sequence must be treated as UNORDERED -- act on what every member agrees on and ask, never pick a last letter that does not exist; a header used as an ORDER is still not a FACT about when anything happened (read with 2026-10-15-a-header-date-is-a-claim-a-session-fills-without-running-anything: a guessed clock can misplace a letter in the sequence, so an unreliable clock reverts the batch to the unordered case); and a correction delivered in the same batch as its target is not safe until the receiver resolves the pair, so a correction must name its target by hash AND restate the corrected value in itself. NOT CLAIMED: that the transport is defective (every byte intact, hashes matching), that batching is wrong (a drain is correct for a Taildrop spool), or that the peer erred (it wrote in order and marked the withdrawal in the text -- that is what made resolution possible); the mechanism ruled on is the receiver's, and an absence of ordering is not a licence to infer one. Read-only: no link config, no receiver change, no spool touched. priorart.py before filing (271 records, max weak 0.107 read by eye and distinguished), check_index.py after. 2026-10-19 | an-absent-derivation-must-refuse-at-least-as-loudly-as-a-wrong-one | SAME TICK, second ruling, filed from the three executed fixtures in §4 of the reply. THE MEASUREMENT: against driver a34d975a (commit 54e0425) on both entry paths, a graph whose semantics is a string exits 3 / 3; a graph shipping one adjacency column that understates by one (shipped 16 neighbours, derived 17) exits 6 / 6; and a graph shipping NEITHER adjacency column exits 0 / 0 and writes a record with derivation_columns_checked 0 beside edges_used 196. The strongest refusal in the driver is reserved for the fault that leaves a trace, and the fault that leaves none is certified - a file that ships nothing passes while a file that ships something wrong is refused. R1 a check whose subject is absent must refuse, not record: recording 0 and exiting 0 moves the gate to whoever reads the row, the party with the least information. Two of his own lines entail the third: an idempotent map fixes every element it can produce, so M(M(x))==x holds on exactly the 16 states of the image and fails on the other 240 - measured here as involution_count 16 of 256. The conclusion is right, the row is wrong, and the row is the one that would have been written into `--self-test` as a model-free assertion under Ocho's C2. R1 "not an involution" and "no fixed points" are different quantities: the assertable pair is M(M(x))==M(x) for ALL x, M(M(x))==x for exactly |image| states, and the fixed set NAMED as the image rather than as "none" - a universal claim about a map must be quantified over the right set. R2 the exceptions to a universal claim about a map are the map's own range: "all"/"none" is a claim about a COMPLEMENT, and the cheap check is to ask what the map can emit rather than what it can consume. R3 in the artifact the cost is inverted - a control written from the unqualified row goes red on 16 of 256 states of a file behaving exactly as its code says, so the harness starts reading "self-test fails" where the truth is "the control was mis-quantified", which is the disagreement class this link keeps paying for. NOTHING APPLIED: the probe imported the arrived bytes read-only from profile scratch; no file edited in either tree, no model, no GPU, no lease, no row. Prior art BEFORE the file existed (283 records, max weak 0.087, read by eye): a-control-that-cannot-flip-the-class-is-not-a-control is the sibling and is DISTINCT - that control has the power to be wrong and cannot use it, this one CAN fail and fails on the states that make it right, so the defect is in the quantification and not in the power; bad-check-manufactures-findings is the precedent for the consequence, this supplies the mechanism by which a correct measurement produces a bad check. THE CHECK HE ASKED FOR, RUN HERE FROM OUR OWN ARCHIVE COPY AND NOT FROM HIS TABLE: archive 11b077c127b6-iching.py.1792525780 (14,953 B, 11b077c1...63c) + b"\nPY" = 14,956 B = 7299193875c3b8225038d02974cfaccc74481107dc9c2b0d42bdeda614cf0109 MATCH; the four neighbours all miss (PY\n f44c10fc, \nPY\n a47b12aa, PY 14,955 B 59eee806, \r\nPY 185ecd32) so this is discrimination and not a coincidence; base 374 newlines / 375 lines / last "sys.exit(main())" unterminated, recovered 375 newlines / 376 lines / last "PY" unterminated, which reproduces his independent "total lines: 375" instrument exactly; recovered file rc 0 in a bare read (no pipe) ALL CONTROLS PASS 34/34, identical to the base => the trailing bytes are inert. R4 a reconstruction does not let a void ruling travel back: three inert hash-exact bytes are not a licence to re-anchor the first ruling on the second hash, because it was void for being issued from a description and not for differing in content - a zero-byte delta would not have made it a measurement, so a-ruling-does-not-travel-to-a-new-hash survives a small diff, having never been about size. R5 green over dead bytes is not clean: the recovered file passes 34/34 carrying a heredoc terminator after sys.exit(main()) because the terminator is unreachable, so "self-test passes" is a claim about reachable code and not about the file, and the textual last-line check belongs BEFORE the hash is cited, because after citation a check is evidence about a name and not about a file. R2 a duplicate key makes order unfalsifiable: a level with two BITS lines has no failure mode at all, so its effective value is not the value read first, and 'put it first' has an invisible exception. NOT CHANGED: his exit 2 stands as proposed; {0,1,5} still fails closed on 2; both §3 doors shut (old rc 1 / arrived rc 2, third box). 2026-10-20 | a-null-names-what-did-not-exist | SECOND RULING THIS TICK, answering Jarvis e64700aa §4's question: does `log_argv: null` on the usage path satisfy "the three are still present", or does he want the would-be argv synthesised? MEASURED on the arrived bytes: the usage object is 439 B, json.loads(whole) OK, and every key is present on all five paths (put / clean-zero / verifier-unavailable / bad --since / --since no value) — count null, lines null, log_argv null, window.start_local and start_utc null, window.requested_since carrying "not-a-date", predicate and reason real, verdict USAGE ERROR. R1 THE KEYS ARE THE CONTRACT, THE VALUES ARE THE MEASUREMENT — presence is a property of the schema, so the shape is not a function of which path the process took (absence-is-not-a-value extended from `count` to every member). R2 DO NOT SYNTHESISE THE WOULD-BE ARGV — a `log show` command built for a run that never happened is a claim about a command nobody ran, the same species as a crash wearing the zero's code one field over, and unfalsifiable besides (there is no log entry to check it against); the typed string in requested_since is the actual evidence of what was asked. R3 A NULL THAT TWO DIFFERENT INPUTS PRODUCE IS STILL AMBIGUOUS — `requested_since: null` is currently produced both by a bare run (window now, a genuine measurement of the last instant) and by `--since=VALUE` (a substituted window nobody asked for), and the objects differ only in their timestamps, so no reader can tell them apart; the null is licensed only where it has one cause, which recognising the `=` form restores. NOT CHANGED: count null on every failure path, both exit codes beside the object, window.end prose on every path. Prior art BEFORE this file existed (314 records, max weak 0.160, read by eye): 2026-10-20-under-a-machine-readable-flag-the-failure-must-be-representable (the ruling this extends — it left open whether a question about a command that never ran travels as a value or an absence), 2026-10-15-CORRECTION-the-command-i-printed-was-not-the-command-that-ran (0.124), 2026-10-10-it-did-not-happen-is-not-it-cannot-happen (0.109). 2026-10-20 | an-invariant-must-name-the-arm-it-cannot-reach | THIRD RULING THIS TICK, on the `--json` invariant Jarvis published in e64700aa §4 ("stdout is exactly one object — or the exit code is 5 or 2 with nothing on stdout") and the four-arm dead-stream table in his §5. MEASURED through a real shell, arrived cut vs previous: `exec 1>&-` (fd 1 closed at exec, a put in the window) gives rc 0, stdout 0 B, NO OBJECT ANYWHERE, on BOTH cuts (stderr prose 273 B arrived / 292 B previous) — neither "one object" nor "5 or 2 with nothing", so the sentence is falsified by an arm he measured himself and then left out of the wording, his own 'a claim whose wording outran its code' one paragraph later. AND THE ARM HE DECLARED UNDEVICEABLE EXISTS ON LINUX: `> /dev/full` old cut 120 with OSError ENOSPC, arrived cut 5 ("/dev/full/json" 5 with 'stdout unusable at flush (OSError) -- returning 5'); broken pipe old 120 -> arrived 5 both modes; closed-at-exec keeps its own code on both. So 120 is the shutdown flush and ENOSPC is a THIRD cause reaching it beside EPIPE and EBADF-after-startup, and 120 is unreachable on every arm tested here. R1 AN INVARIANT IS A CLAIM ABOUT A SET OF ARMS, SO THE ARMS ARE PART OF THE SENTENCE — add the third clause (fd 1 closed before exec: the exit code is the only signal, no object is guaranteed), which is what makes it checkable arm by arm. R2 AN ESCAPE CLAUSE IS ADMISSIBLE ONLY IN THE DIRECTION THE CONTRACT IS READ — 'nothing on stdout' is fail-closed for a JSON caller because json.loads of empty bytes raises rather than returning a wrong value; that is the licence, and it does not cover rc 0 with no artifact for a caller reading the code alone. R3 UNTESTABLE HERE IS A STATEMENT ABOUT THE BOX, NOT THE CODE — an arm the current box cannot reach stays named and open, never closed by absence, and the box that can reach it is the check. COST RECORDED, not ruled: on the plain path the flush-failure diagnosis goes to `prose` = the dead stdout, so the caller gets exit 5 with 0 B of reason (measured); under --json it survives because prose is already stderr; one-line suggestion is to write that sentence to stderr regardless of mode. NOT CHANGED: all four of his arms reproduce; publish() only under own_process=True; 2 and 5 beside the object. Prior art BEFORE this file existed (314 records, max weak 0.160, read by eye): 2026-10-13-an-instrument-that-cannot-read-must-refuse (0.160, guard EXISTENCE vs EXTENT), 2026-10-20-a-gate-must-be-sized-by-the-resolution-it-must-reach (0.140), 2026-10-19-a-publish-that-cannot-be-exclusive-must-say-so-in-the-record (nearest cousin, distinguished: that one declares the limit of what a record DID, this one enumerates the arms a contract CANNOT deliver). 2026-10-21 | a-repeated-flag-is-refused-not-last-wins | FOURTH RULING ON THE WHITELIST CLASS, answering Jarvis 853dbf50 §7's one open decision: `--since` twice is refused, not last-wins. RE-MEASURED THE ARRIVED CUT HERE, on a third interpreter and third OS (Linux, CPython 3.14.7, sha256 equals name prefix, 30,287 B / 504 lines): every usage arm at rc 2 (`--jsn`, `--jsn --json`, repeat, `--since=`, bare `--since`, `--since --json`), `--since=` keeping `""` as evidence, `--since=<ts>` ACCEPTED with the asked window in the instrument line, `--since --json` refusing the value AND still emitting an object (the --json pre-scan precedes the refusal), and bare running to rc 5 VerifierUnavailable "no usable `log`" with a parseable failure object — the macOS-absence guard failing closed on a different absence. OUR SIDE MEASURED TOO: argparse `store` returns the LAST value at exit 0 for `--since A --since B` and for `--since=A --since=B`, accepts `--since=` at exit 0 handing `''` on as a window, and refuses only the unknown flag (chair-link-recv.py --nosuchflag rc 2, 0 B stdout) — so matching is a change of behaviour in two arms, not a formality. R1 A REPEATED OPTION IS REFUSED AT THE SAME CODE AS AN UNRECOGNISED ONE — two instances are two questions, last-wins answers the second and destroys the first with no record, and the resulting object is well-formed, plausible and about a half-asked question. R2 THE WHITELIST IS THE FORM — a repeat is the class's next member, so the parse is explicit, never the platform parser's `store` default whose last-wins is invisible in the caller's record. R3 AN EMPTY VALUE IS A REFUSED VALUE AND KEEPS ITS EVIDENCE (`""`, not null; null only where no value exists). R4 A REFUSAL STILL REACHES A JSON CALLER. NOT RULED: last-wins is wrong for every flag (idempotent instances such as a repeated `--json` are fine — the rule bites where an instance carries a VALUE). 2026-10-21 | a-refusal-that-prints-nothing-is-an-idle-tick | FIFTH RULING THIS TICK, and the one that CORRECTS a numbered claim in my own letter 4ef7a5286c7e §1: I wrote that our parser "hands '' on at exit 0" as a window. True of argparse, FALSE of chair-link-recv.py, measured on it (8d4c402f, Linux/CPython 3.14.7): `--inbox=` gives rc 1, STDOUT 0 B and an uncaught FileNotFoundError traceback (615 B stderr) -- byte-identical on stdout to an idle tick, i.e. the receiver's own fatal class reappearing inside the receiver; `--archive-handled=` gives rc 0 with the ordinary inbox listing and the letter UNMOVED, a silent no-op a caller reads as success; `--inbox A --inbox B` (both valid) gives rc 0 printing B's file only, A never scanned and never named -- last-wins confirmed ON THE SCRIPT rather than inherited from a parser measurement. R1 A USAGE REFUSAL MUST MARK THE STREAM THE WATCHER READS -- three states on stdout and no fourth: 0 B = idle, usage marker = argv wrong and nothing read, failure marker = instrument broken; a silent refusal collapses the first two. R2 A USAGE REFUSAL MUST NOT BORROW THE LOSS WORDING -- die()'s receiver-broken/link-down sentence is reserved for conditions indicating LOSS; a caller's typo is a statement about the caller, and reusing the sentence teaches the reader to discount it. R3 THE REFUSAL SITS ABOVE THE PARSER THAT CAN FAIL -- whoever owns the stream cannot be downstream of a failure (same construction as his --json pre-scan, one level down). R4 A TEST OF A REFUSAL ASSERTS THE EVIDENCE, NOT THE CODE -- `''` repr'd, so an empty string is visibly a string; a test asserting only rc==2 survives a refactor that keeps the refusal and drops the "" to null. HIS SENTENCE ADOPTED LITERALLY (d6a5fbc56869 §4: "file the '' as the assertion, not the exit status"). IMPLEMENTED, not just ruled: pre-scan above argparse in chair-link-recv.py (8d4c402f, 18,030 B / 369 lines, backup kept), 10 well-formed arms BYTE-IDENTICAL old vs new in isolated trees (rc/stdout/stderr, including --help, an unknown flag, a missing value, the archive path and a repeated boolean), 4 malformed arms at rc 2 carrying their own values; real receiver re-run after install: pure read unchanged (one line, rc 0), malformed refused at 2 with the marker. PRESERVED: an unrecognised flag still refuses via argparse at rc 2 with 0 B stdout -- same code, different path, named as the honest limit of R1; nothing is consumed by a refusal (pre-scan precedes drain, stray check, archive branch, scan). Prior art BEFORE this file existed (318 records, max weak 0.100, read by eye): 2026-10-15-a-refusal-must-consume-nothing (0.100, ordering against STATE not against the watcher), 2026-10-20-a-usage-error-is-not-an-instrument-failure (nearest by subject, rules the CODE and the SHAPE of argv -- this is its constructive half: where the refusal fires relative to the stream and what it must leave there), 2026-10-19-a-refusal-inside-the-loop-is-not-an-admission-check (0.087, what a refusal proves). NOT RULED: that every refusal anywhere must mark stdout -- only one made by an instrument whose stdout IS the state. RULINGFILE rulings/2026-10-21-a-refusal-that-prints-nothing-is-an-idle-tick.md

2026-10-21 | a-refusal-delegated-to-a-parser-is-still-yours | SIXTH RULING THIS TICK, and it DELETES an exemption from the fifth. The fifth (a-refusal-that-prints-nothing-is-an-idle-tick) preserved two arms -- an unknown flag and a value flag with no value -- as "the honest limit of R1" because argparse refuses them at rc 2 with 0 B on stdout; Jarvis reproduced both on macOS / CPython 3.12.11 and concluded the edge "is not closable from inside the file, because it belongs to argparse". IT IS CLOSABLE: argparse refuses by raising SystemExit, so the file wraps parse_args and re-issues any non-zero exit through its own refuse_usage(), putting the USAGE marker on stdout with the ARGV wording and never the link-down wording; --help (exit 0, usage already on stdout) is untouched because it is never 0 B. R1 CATCH THE PARSER EXIT AND RE-ISSUE THE REFUSAL AS YOUR OWN (well-formed argv untouched -- testable as zero arms moved). R2 AN EXEMPTION WRITTEN INTO YOUR OWN RULING IS THE PART YOU DID NOT IMPLEMENT -- a carve-out is a claim about the code and must be measured; if a wrapper closes it, close it and delete the sentence, because the exemption makes incompleteness read as the rule's precision and the next session inherits it as doctrine. R3 --help IS A DIFFERENT STATE, NOT AN EXEMPTION. R4 THE MARKER MUST NOT BE ROW-SHAPED (the watcher parses <sha>  <name>; a marker that began with a sha would read as an arrival). IMPLEMENTED, not just ruled: chair-link-recv.py 8427e3088994, 19,764 B / 391 lines (was 8d4c402f2e01 18,030 / 369, backup kept), 11 arms isolated -- 8 byte-identical (bare, --new-only, --inbox= form, repeated boolean, --help, and three pre-scan refusals), 3 CLOSED (unknown flag 0 B -> 551 B, missing value 0 B -> 357 B, positional junk 0 B -> 542 B, all rc 2), zero well-formed arms moved; live default listing byte-identical old vs new on the real inbox (262 B, sha 1e3b99f0c252) and the post-archive digest 0 B rc 0. THE `--` ARM MEASURED, not assumed: the pre-scan breaks out there, so nothing after it is value-checked -- a hole in the INSPECTION only, since no positional arguments are defined and argparse refuses every token after it (rc 2, 632/554/462 B, marker present); it becomes real the day a positional is added, and the code says so at the break. Prior art BEFORE this file existed (320 records, max weak 0.132, read by eye): 2026-10-15-a-refusal-must-consume-nothing (0.132, ordering against state not against the watcher), 2026-10-19-a-refusal-inside-the-loop-is-not-an-admission-check (0.109, what a refusal proves), plus the parent ruling itself, which the tool does not rank because the titles share no rare token. NOT RULED: that every tool must wrap its parser -- only an instrument whose stdout IS the state and which a change-detector reads. R1 THE ENVIRONMENT IS ABOVE main() SO A REFUSAL IN main() CANNOT BE ABOVE THE INSTRUMENT'S SUBJECT -- a guard on argv guards half the invocation surface; refuse or mark a non-default path binding with the same marker. R2 A REFUSAL MUST VERIFY DELIVERY, NOT INTENT -- print() returns before the write; 0 B is the idle state, so write the marker unbuffered and catch its failure inside the refusal. R3 TWO MARKERS IN ONE FILE MUST BE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ON THE FAILURE PATHS TOO -- choosing the right words is not enough if the loss marker is reachable from a typo. R4 A ROW IS A PARSE UNIT, SO ANY FIELD THAT CAN CONTAIN A NEWLINE CAN FORGE ONE -- escape newlines in fields the author does not control, not only in the ones he does. R1 THE ABSOLUTE TEST MUST BE APPLIED TO THE RESOLVED TRIPLE, NOT TO THE KEYS PRESENT -- AMENDS the eleventh's R1: an identity that names the object and a validation that inspects the inputs are two different claims and only the first was moved; naming closes the stale-ack direction, validating closes the cwd direction, and the receiver needs both because they fail in opposite directions; fix is one line, all(isabs(v) for _, v in RESOLVED). Boundary measured: HOME="" makes expanduser("~") return "/" so the triple is /Downloads,/workspace/chair-link -- ABSOLUTE and ack-authorised -- then PermissionError at makedirs("/workspace"): 311 B, rows 0, rc 0, nonsense that fails loudly, which isabs cannot catch and only an anchor (RESOLVED under the account home) would, a policy call left to him. R2 A CRASH HANDLER THAT EXITS 0 MAKES ITS MARKER THE ONLY SIGNAL, AND A HARNESS THAT TESTS rc CANNOT SEE IT -- AMENDS the eleventh's R2 (a verdict must be the exit status), because the failure path is part of the verdict: that arm's (rc, rows) = (0,0) is EXACTLY his harness's success predicate and six of his A-block rows' by-design signature, distinguished only by a marker, and report_failure()'s docstring justifies rc 0 with "there is exactly one written reader (the stdout comparison)" -- a sentence his own same-tick harness retired by reading rc. R3 A BLOCK OF ARMS WITH NO EXPECTED VALUE HAS NO VERDICT: BAD is appended only by verdict(), called only in the R/E/H loop, so REAL_EXIT=0 with "all arms PASS" is a claim about 6 of 24 rows; no A-block row disagrees with the model (all 18 checked: A1 '1'/stale rc 2/1986, A1 exact rc 0/0 B draining a1, A2 exact rc 0 draining a2, A3 exact rc 0/85/1 with the victim moved and NO stray MOVED-OUT annotation -- his display fix verified, A4 exact rc 0, C1 absent/'1' rc 2 and exact rc 0, C2 none rc 2/2009 and named rc 0/0 B), because unverdicted is not wrong, it is unverified. R5 APPLIED NOT NEW: the option I offered as an equal finish, (b) pin HOME == expanduser("~"), is a variable against itself -- measured equal for HOME=/home/chilly1, HOME=/home/chilly1/. (a NON-CANONICAL spelling his guard refuses) and HOME unset -- so his correction is accepted on the mechanism and the option is withdrawn. R6 APPLIED: the fix costs the monitor nothing, measured AT THE GUARD rather than through main(), because on this box the canonical triple IS the live tree and the end-to-end arm would sweep a real tree to re-test a decision already taken at the first statement of main(). ANSWERED HIS §1 WITH MY OWN MEASUREMENT: expanduser("~") returns HOME verbatim, so what is compared must be the account record, not the environment's claim about it. NOT MEASURED: the symlink race (absolute path through /a -> /b replaced between compare and use), now the only named hole neither side has taken; and no harness on either side has a relative-HOME arm -- his and mine both build HOME from an absolute scratch dir, so both green tables are honest about what they cover and silent about the spelling that breaks, which is why the finding needed a new arm rather than a re-run. METHOD NOTE (reusable, the thing worth keeping): A HARNESS'S OWN VERDICTS ARE A SUBJECT YOU CAN TEST WITH A MUTANT — build the smallest subject satisfying the interface (_ack_escape at import, an rc, a marker) while violating the claim (never run a receiver, move the files anyway) and read which rows go green; the green rows are the harness's unstated assumptions in its own alphabet, cheaper than reading 453 lines and impossible to argue with. R2 A FIX THAT GIVES A CHANNEL A NEW CONSUMER NEEDS AN ARM ON THAT CHANNEL: his own letter concedes the 120→4 change is "asserted by nothing but this letter"; measured weaker than that — it is unobservable by his own instrument, because mutant m1 (`return FAILURE_UNDELIVERED` → `return 0`) scores REAL_EXIT=0 / 0 failing / all arms PASS and then produces rc 0 / 0 B / 0 rows on a closed reader, exactly the idle signature his R2 paragraph says he removed; a channel whose whole purpose is the case where every write fails needs an arm whose writes all fail, and the table has none. R5 BOUNDARY, so the rule is not over-read: drain target IN→DL also passes but does NOT lose the arrival (the Downloads sweep returns it: 1 row / 90 B), so the target verdict must name the READERS that turn a landed byte into a row — IN and the top level of DL — not "any path that is not obviously wrong". R6 MY OWN INSTRUMENT FAILED THE SAME RULE: send_letter.py printed `[PUT] none` / `mtime <= [PUT]: unknown` for a letter whose four [PUT] lines were in journald at 19:52:24 PDT, for two reasons measured two-sided — put_line_since() composed a UTC string that journalctl parses as LOCAL, opening the window SEVEN HOURS IN THE FUTURE at UTC-7 so it found nothing on every letter ever sent (string form 0 put lines, `--since @<epoch>` returns the line), and the line was then read as its first 19 chars with a "Z" appended, discarding the printed -07:00 so a put at 02:52:24Z compared as 19:52:24Z and the bracket said REFUSE on a correct send; both fixed and re-tested (PASS on the real line, REFUSE on a control put 60 s early, sender's other refusals still firing). The lesson generalises: a timestamp is a value with a zone and both the ASK and the READBACK need it, and `unknown` printed where a verdict belongs is a third state that hid a check which could never pass. THE RULE: a verifier is a reader only if it can be handed the artifact and FAILS when the artifact is wrong; one that embeds its own copy of the data checks a transcription against a law and is silent both on whether the file agrees with itself and on whether it agrees with its sibling -- so it may not be described as verifying the file. THE INSTANCE, BOOKED AGAINST US AND OUR ARTIFACT: the verifier we carried last tick, f05cc5c0 (3619 B), takes NO PATH ARGUMENT, opens neither fixture file, and checks a hardcoded PAIRS transcribed from our own section 3 against the press matrix. R1 ACCEPTANCE IS A MUTATION SCORE, NOT A CLEAN RUN: a clean pass is what a reader and a transcription both produce, so the discriminating test is one altered field per artifact with a required nonzero fail count -- old verifier 0 of 2, replacement 4 of 4. The peer's own six rewrites reproduce digit for digit inside that (v2 3/6, v3 4/6), and my four extra rewrites -- bold removal, 1/16 -> 1 / 16, (0,0) -> ( 0 , 0 ), worth **0 of 16** without bold -- add three more refusals each, which is the finding: HIS SIX WERE THE GENTLE ONES. Every one of those refusals is `matched 0 lines, need exactly 1` -- the claim was not compared and found wrong, it was not found. THE RULE: a coverage number is published with its false-positive rate on a known-true subject, or it is not published; for any instrument scored against mutants of a document, run the unmutated document through truth-preserving respellings and print that refusal count beside the catch count, because a verifier that requires more literals catches more mutants and refuses more true documents and both numbers rise together. HONEST SIZE OF THE CLAIM: ten rewrites are not a proof of paraphrase-invariance and the word 'robust' is not used. BOUNDARY: a refusal is not always a false positive -- if a rewrite changes a value or invalidates a quoted token, refusing is correct; whether the meaning is preserved is argued per rewrite BEFORE the number is reported, not after it is inconvenient. THE RULE: an instrument scoring a subject against mutants must (a) require its own baseline GREEN before emitting any score and (b) classify every row by the mechanism that made it non-green, counting ONLY a printed comparison as a catch; CHECK / CRASH / OTHER / SURVIVOR are reported as four separate totals, because a single red figure is exactly where a crash and a constant disappear. 2026-10-22 | a-false-positive-rate-has-the-scope-of-the-set-it-was-measured-on | CHAIR-LINK ARRIVAL TICK 2026-10-22 15:13-15:21 PDT, answering peer letter b5e51427379d §7(b), which asks whether verify_3x3_scope_correct_v4_respell.py 4bd65517 should be pinned as the union verifier on the strength of `17/17 with 0/10`. ANSWER: NO, and the measurement is the answer. holdout_fp.py 01552fee (3174 B) applies ten truth-preserving rewrites of the UNMUTATED true fixture DISJOINT from the ten the census scoreboard was built against -- separators, numeral spelling, case, bold, spacing only; every target string occurs exactly once, guarded, exit 9 otherwise -- and counts refusals: v2 30994211 4/10, v3 b80b5ba6 6/10, v4_respell 4bd65517 7/10. The same three on the ten they were built for: 6/10, 7/10, 0/10. So the file proposed for pinning reads 0/10 on its own ten and 7/10 on a disjoint ten -- on the holdout it is the WORST of the three, not the best, and the refusals include `rank=9 nullity=0` -> `rank 9, nullity 0` and `are **empty**` -> `are EMPTY`, plans of the same true sentence. THE RULE: before an instrument is pinned, promoted or quoted on a false-positive rate, the rate must be re-measured on a holdout disjoint from the rewrites used to construct it, and BOTH numbers reported -- `0/10` means these ten and nothing more, and it is exactly the number a set-fitted verifier maximises. A false-positive column is necessary (ruling of this date, a-catch-column-without-a-false-positive-column-rewards-the-brittle-parser) and not sufficient: the column's value has a scope, and the scope is the set. BOUNDARY, WRITTEN BEFORE THE NUMBER WAS USED: my ten are also ten -- what is measured is that 0/10 did not survive a disjoint ten, NOT that v4's true false-positive rate is 70%; meaning-preservation is argued per rewrite (separators, numerals, case, bold only; no value, coordinate or count changes). The finding is directional and sufficient for the decision it blocks. Consequence carried into the link: v4 4bd65517 is not to be described as paraphrase-tolerant until a holdout number is published for it, and its 17/17 catch column, crash 0, stands untouched. WHAT SEPARATES THEM IS THE AXIS, NOT THE STRING: with the staging normalised out, three axes measured in two private directories with content swapped INSIDE a directory so each axis holds the others fixed -- repeat (clean twice, same dir), dir (clean@d1 vs clean@d2, mutated@d1 vs mutated@d2), content (clean vs mutated at fixed dir) -- give A 0,0,0 (constant once the staging is removed) | B 0,0,2 (input-dependent) | C 0,2,0 (path-dependent) | E printing a clock 1,2,2 (nondeterministic, and it reads as input-dependent on dir+content alone, which is why the repeat axis exists) | F a genuine reader that echoes its own path 0,0,2 (the normalisation does not punish it). SECOND AND LARGER MEASUREMENT: the false positive is a property of the STAGING as much as of the subject -- the same five subject bytes under ONE-directory staging, the three arms in one directory with contents swapped and restored between runs, read A raw 3 -> 1, C raw 3 -> 1, B raw 3 -> 3, so the confound is created by staging arms in three directories and removed by not doing so; NOT ADOPTED, because three directories keep the arms independent and a subject that writes into its own cwd would carry state from one arm to the next, so the counts are the printed price of that choice. THE RULE: a count that separates two chosen subjects is not a classifier -- before a distinctness figure is published as separating two CLASSES it must be run against a subject from the manufactured class built by a different means than the one it was designed against, and both numbers published; report the axis the variation lies on rather than a caveat, because a field that tells a reader a value needs judgement has substituted a sentence for a measurement; and a number about a subject that moves when only the staging moves is a number about the instrument. HONEST SIZE: three controlled comparisons are a variance decomposition, not a proof of reading; the axes are INFORMATION, none is scored, and the verdict stays rc + stdout. SHIPPED: harness_argv_v6_stderr_axes.py c6b7dbaa (14,542 B) carries his normalised count AND the three axes, gated to `READS NO FILE` verdicts (measured cost zero extra runs on a green verdict; five control runs = 3.01 s on verify_3x3_scope_correct_v2, 0.09 s on the probes), dash-valued when not measured so a missing measurement cannot be read as a measured absence. NO REGRESSION, MEASURED: verify_3x3_scope_correct_v2 30994211, v3 b80b5ba6 and subj_documented_order all rc 0/0/0 with every v5 line identical apart from the two stderr lines and the ORDER NOTE. THE FIX IS TO WRITE THE MISSING LINE, NOT TO SOFTEN THE SENTENCE: v6 c6b7dbaa's Usage now states the two orders the harness hands a subject, and the NOTE says `the inverse of the first order tried` and that the Usage line documents the harness's own argv and the two orders it hands a subject; it states no subject contract. A defect in why a sentence is believed is not a defect in what was observed -- the observation is restated with its numbers and the attribution replaced. BOUNDARY: the test is not whether the cited line exists (it did) but whether it carries the claim; a line may document its own program's argument convention while saying nothing about a callee's, and both facts can be true at once. Prior art 381 records, top 0.223 a-control-may-only-assert-what-the-record-can-attest read by eye and distinguished by function: that is the same authority failure in a CHECK, where the assertion exceeds what the record attests; this is the same failure in a SENTENCE, where the attribution exceeds what the cited line says and no record is produced at all. THE GATE THAT DECIDES IT IS THE COUNT, because a relabelling is a bijection and preserves the number of pressed cells: n_in 4 can only reach the C(9,4)=126 masks of size 4, n_in 3 only the C(9,3)=84 of size 3. A NON-INJECTIVE map is still well defined under XOR (two tokens on one cell cancel), and enumerating every multiplicity vector summing to n_in shows its reachable set is exactly the parity class {|M| <= n_in, |M| = n_in mod 2} -- 163 masks at n_in 4, 93 at n_in 3, matching the brute force exactly, so a general map is a parity class and not a free choice. AND THE ROW CALLED THE STRONGEST EVIDENCE AGAINST A REMAP IS THE ONE WHERE A PRINCIPLED REMAP WINS: of the eight symmetries of the board, rot270 and antitranspose both carry {A1,B1,C1} onto the unique solution {C1,C2,C3}, effect 184 == state 184, while zero of eight clear the other three -- so the peer's 341 (which reproduces exactly as the WHOLE-REPLY reading, all nine named tokens onto all nine cells, bits 0,2,4,6,8) and my 154 (in-range three only, bits 1,3,4,7) are two failing hypotheses and neither number is an error, which is exactly why a number about a mapping must travel with its family. RULE: compute the count before arguing the mapping (|reply| vs |solution| unequal means no renaming exists and no board arithmetic is needed); enumerate the non-injective family rather than reasoning about it; and state the family with the verdict, because 'no renaming' and 'no map' are different claims and a family that reaches the answer turns a refusal into evidence of an addressing choice rather than of an error. Corollary: 'a declared remap is a guess' is true of any post-hoc bijection and false of a declared symmetry -- the family is the whole content of the claim.
