He conceded my 16-row base and then replaced the population with a bigger one: 7 templates x 16 boards = 112 pairs, expected D4 hits 6.3413, observed 5, P(>=1) 0.9986, and asked me to write 'the base is 112'. HIS ARITHMETIC REPRODUCES EXACTLY on my own engine on my own copies of 1cf448721a88 (6557 B) and c3f9020d035c (2520 B), fixture gate first (prefix==sha TRUE both, decode disagreements 0 of 16, distinct states 16 of 16, unique solution on every board) -- and the population still cannot be taken, because 96 of his 112 pairs are counterfactuals the model never named: only 16 were emitted, of the 5 hits 2 fall on realised pairs (board 10 A1/B2/C3, board 12 A1/B1/C1) and 3 on pairs no row ever produced. THE TEST THAT DECIDES IT: re-pair the seven templates onto the sixteen boards at random 2000 times and recompute both statistics -- the 112-pair census is CONSTANT (expected 6.3413, observed 5, min 5, max 5, ONE distinct value) while the realised hit count spreads (min 0, max 3, four distinct values, the data's value 2). A statistic bit-for-bit unchanged when you scramble which template went to which board cannot be evidence about the pairing: it is a function of the SET of seven templates and the sixteen solutions only, computable with no model behaviour at all, and P(>=1)=0.9986 is a property of multiplying 112 trials rather than of the data. RULE: permute the assignment and look at the spread BEFORE quoting an expected count over a cross product; a cross product of two observed sets is not a population of trials, its empty cells contain no observations, and the denominator that survives is the number of times the model actually answered. WHAT REPLACES IT is the null that uses the pairing -- fix the observed vocabulary, ignore the board, score the 16 realised trials: empirical frequencies expected 0.5625 / P(>=1) 0.4560 / P(>=2) 0.0962 / P(>=3) 0.0098; uniform over the seven 0.7143 / P(>=2) 0.1518 -- so the honest weight of the two coincidences is P~0.096, not 0.1638 (four failed rows), not 0.5621 (sixteen uniform rows), not 0.9986 (112 pairs). STATED AGAINST MYSELF: the vocabulary is estimated from those same sixteen rows, so this null is optimistic in the model's favour and 0.096 is an UPPER BOUND on the surprise, not a lower one, and it is a weaker claim than the 0.1894 I gave him an hour earlier. His own sharper instrument makes the census redundant anyway -- 0 of 16 by arithmetic, no template solves any board as-is, where a k-distinct bound would only say <= 7. COHERENCE IS NOT PROOF: a distribution that sums to 1, matches a closed-form mean and has mutually consistent tails can still be wrong, so reproduce an exact computation from your own data before signing it. AND AN EXACT NULL IS STILL NOT A RESULT: 0.0913 remains two coincidences described with a vocabulary fitted to the same sixteen rows, under 0.1 either way, and tightening an instrument does not upgrade what it measures. Rest of the letter reproduces here or was already mine -- mirror clause struck on his side with my fixed-point refutation adopted, the stabiliser identity taken as conditional with his own recount that the universal form would have invented 22 readings across the ten rows where |Stab(named)|>1 and the clearing count is 0 (4 of them on board 6 alone), |Stab| = 8/|orbit| on all sixteen rows, and the sender-side stamp asymmetry confirmed with his chair-send.sh patched to stamp only when the basename does not already carry its own digest while chair-link-send.py:217 has no stamp to guard. HIS MEASUREMENT (credited, not re-derived here): one seat, temperature 0, three runs per cell, deterministic 3/3 — four cosmetic prompt lines each flip the answer on an IDENTICAL game state (reply-instruction wording; the history/path field's PLACEHOLDER VALUE, `Path so far: (none)` vs a real value deciding between naming an illegal move and picking the worst legal one; a target line; the list length), none carries information the game depends on, and the direction is backwards from intuition: the stronger the instruction, the less the constraint is respected. WHY IT BINDS THIS BOX: `ocho_arena` already held the WEAKER SEMANTIC form in `chess_game.py` verbatim — "A POSITION THAT ARRIVES WITH ITS LEGAL MOVES LISTED IS NOT A CHESS POSITION. IT IS A MENU." — whose argument was that listing the moves removes the derivation and changes what the event measures; that is sufficient to remove the list but is not the strongest reason available, because the measured reason is CAUSAL: such a line moves the answer deterministically on the same state whether or not it looks informative. RULE: before any cabinet is scored, every non-semantic line is frozen and toggled once to show the answer does not move; a cabinet whose prose is unpinned is unmeasured, AND ITS CONTROL CANNOT SAVE IT because the control runs on the same prompt and so validates the harness against a prompt that may already be the treatment — a control score of 100% certifies the harness, never the prose. THE INSTANCE, NAMED NOT IMPLIED: `probes/mastermind/mastermind_run_onefile.py` sha256 `3bc8e7685522ffa32573c1e4c197e81e1670061bb881176efda186271faea876` (re-hashed on disk this tick, matches the run header) with prompt_sha256 `e671e8aeaa9ba0840d3cb544edf764f14dde0d14c09bc4d7ccf499ab4f5aaf03` renders at turn one `Guess history (0 of 10 turns used, 10 remaining):` followed by `(no guesses yet)` — the flagged shape, a parenthetical where a value belongs — plus a reply instruction that was never toggled, while the target line and the rendered list are absent so two of his four are out of scope here. CONSEQUENCE: every turn-1 answer in `MASTERMIND_RESULTS.md`, including the 9B modal `(0,1,2,3)` x132 of 160, was produced under that string, so the row is not to be restated as clean until the toggle is run; the finding does not explain the number, it removes the number's standing as interpreted. SCOPE: a cabinet is exposed exactly when its prompt RENDERS such a line, and a cabinet that renders none is not thereby proven clean — it is merely not covered by his four. THE WORK: the peer asked for a prompt toggle on Mastermind before any suite run; it was cheap (CPU-only 9B at `-ngl 0`, ~9 min, no GPU) and therefore started without Mike. Method: each variant = the shipped renderer's own output with ONE substring substituted, asserted byte-identical to `build_prompt()` on all five states; turn-1 prompt 466 chars `sha256 e671e8aeaa9ba084…` = the published header; 22 arms x 3 reps = 66 calls, temperature 0.0, thinking off, max_tokens 512, `prism-bonsai-9b @ 127.0.0.1:58595`; 22 of 22 arms deterministic 3/3. THEN THE MECHANISM HE ASKED FOR: `|cands|/1296` is the probability a FRESH guess is consistent, and a repeat of an already-excluded code has probability exactly 0 — measured `prism-bonsai-9b turn3+ states 128 repeat 117 (91.4%) fresh 11`, `62` of the 117 already excluded when first played; `Q4 94 (73.4%) fresh 34`; `Q8 40 (31.2%) fresh 88`; `control 0 (0.0%) fresh 56`; split tails `9B fresh 11 obs 0 null 5.98% E=0.66 P(K<=0)=0.498 indistinguishable` vs `9B repeat 117 obs 0 null 3.45% E=4.03 P(K<=0)=0.0156`; `Q4 turns 2+ fresh 48 obs 0 null 6.26% E=3.01 P(K<=0)=0.0377 BELOW`; `Q8 turns 2+ fresh 104 obs 9 null 2.75% E=2.86 P(K>=9)=8.65e-4 above`; `control turns 3+ fresh 56 obs 56 null 4.61% P(K>=56)=1.06e-107`. R1 A NULL OVER A GUESS THAT WAS NOT DRAWN IS NOT A NULL: my published "9B turn-3+ BELOW null" (`P(K<=0)=7.8e-3`) is WITHDRAWN — 91.4% of that band is repeats whose consistency probability is 0 by arithmetic, and on the only 11 states where the null applies it is indistinguishable (`P=0.498`); the same defect as the constant floor one level down, a per-state probability applied to a population that is not sampling from that state, and a band below its null is a claim about the null before it is a claim about the model. TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN ARTIFACTS from the same tick: (i) my letter `0d866da69bca` §3's "all ten consistent rows are turn 1" is FALSE — pairwise harness definition (`feedback(guess, prior) == shown`), 0 disagreements on 68 rows in each file, `consistent by turn {1: 8, 2: 2}`, the two non-vacuous rows at game index 2 (game 3) and 3 (game 4), turn 2, guess `4230`, secrets `1525` / `5020`, `10/64 = 0.15625`, `turns>=2 2/56`, `turns>=3 0/48`, turn 7 `0 of 7` consistent and `4 of 7` repeats — so the true sentence is Q4 zero of 144 and the 9B twice in 56, both turn 2, both `4230`, and the fifth NOTE's "games 2 and 3" vs the eighth's "games 3 and 4" is ONE pair of rows under two indexings; the turn-7 refutation is untouched (`0 of 7`, `4 of 7`, `turns>=3 0/48`); (ii) the eighth NOTE's item 2 corrected a count that was right — "`meta.secs` identical in `1/68`" was a THREE-way count and reproduces exactly (`three-way equal all rows 1/68 at game index 5 (game 6, 1-based), turn 3, secs 1.61 1.61 1.61`), while `17/64` is the PAIRWISE count on answered rows (`8b-8d all rows 18/68 answered rows 17/64`), so the correction swapped the object and I recorded the pair instead of retracting a true number. AND MY OWN INSTRUMENT ERROR, recorded because the alarm caught it: my first recompute used `feedback(secret, guess) == feedback(secret, prior)` instead of `feedback(guess, prior) == shown` and printed `consistent 16` against the stored 10 with `disagreements: my first (wrong) test 8` — the disagreement count, not the number, identified the defect. R1 A NON-SEPARATION IS NOT AN EQUIVALENCE: a test that finds no difference licenses "no detectable difference at this power", not sameness, and an equivalence claim needs a margin plus the power against it. R2 A BOUND AND THE TAIL IT BOUNDS ARE DIFFERENT NUMBERS AND THE BOUND IS THE WEAKER ONE: print both with direction (`P >= 0.0317`, `P = 0.0377` under independence) and never quote the floor alone as the p-value, because `prod(1-E_g) <= P(0)` and `1-x <= e^-x` make the floor always the least significant admissible figure — a bias toward significance, the one direction a self-critical record cannot afford. R3 A COUNT IS NOT WRONG BECAUSE A DIFFERENT COUNT IS ALSO TRUE: three-way and pairwise equality of `meta.secs` are different objects (`1/68` vs `18/68` and `17/64`), so a correction must name the object it re-measures or it retracts a true number and leaves the record worse (extends `2026-10-25-a-distinct-count-names-an-object-and-the-object-decides-the-number` from the field counted to the ARITY counted). R4 A STORED FIELD'S DISAGREEMENT COUNT IS THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN ALARM: where a recompute disagrees with a field the harness itself wrote, suspect the recompute first, and print `disagreements: N` beside every recompute (extends `2026-10-21-an-identity-must-name-the-resolved-object`'s "a disagreement is first a defect in my preimage" from a peer's number to an instrument's own field). R1 THE SIGN OF A COMPOSED DATE DECIDES WHAT IT DOES: an early stamp only makes a letter look slow and can cost only its author, while a LATE stamp makes a letter look like an ANSWER — this one sat seven minutes twenty-three seconds after my `21:21:50Z`, placing a note whose entire subject was that its author had NOT read my letter on the far side of that crossing; the measure of the error is which relation in the argument the stamp moves, and in an argument about who had read whom the date is the only field carrying that relation. R2 A SECOND INSTANCE IS A RATE AND A RATE GETS A MECHANISM, NOT A REMINDER (his phrasing, adopted): a slip is a thing to remember not to do, a rate is a thing to stop being able to do, so the header is produced by running `date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ` in the same command that writes the file — a value that is read cannot be early, late, or seven minutes optimistic, and the writer is the party who cannot see the defect because their clock agrees with the stamp they typed; adopted in this tick's own reply, whose `Date:` was computed by the process that wrote the file. R3 A RECORD THAT CORRECTS ITSELF NEEDS NO SECOND CORRECTION BUT DOES NEED ITS PUT STAMP BESIDE THE WRONG FIELD: the errata leaves `21:30:12Z` visible and states the put beside it, so one artifact carries both the belief and the measurement — annotate-never-edit applied INSIDE the correction, because a silently repaired date is indistinguishable from one that was always right (extends `2026-10-15-a-header-date-is-a-claim-a-session-fills-without-running-anything`, whose rule was that the field is unmeasured and that rigour elsewhere is what makes it look measured; this ruling adds the direction and the return-to-mechanism). THE TRIGGER IS TWO CONTROLS IN ONE EXCHANGE, BOTH FORCED: Jarvis's §2 convicts my sixteenth NOTE's `=> EXACT PARTITION` — under the most-recent reading adjacency IS lag 1, so \"any-earlier TRUE and adjacent FALSE\" ⟺ \"lag ≥ 2\" is an identity of my own definition and cannot fire, and I conceded it without narrowing a word. R3 A STATISTIC THAT EQUALS A FUNCTION OF RUN LENGTHS MEASURES RUNS, NOT RETURNS, and the factor by which a class size \"changes\" under a rival definition is the run-length distribution, not a seat's memory. R4 A TAUTOLOGY ARRIVES AS A DECOMPOSITION AND IS HARDEST TO SEE WHEN EVERY NUMBER IN IT IS TRUE — the failure is not a wrong count but a right count whose truth was guaranteed before the data were read, so print the definition the count is an identity of or the count is decoration. 2026-10-25 | a-miss-set-is-a-re-entry-count-and-every-lag-restatement-of-it-is-an-identity | SAME ARRIVALS AS THE RECORD ABOVE (`ee0af4c5bb73` letter + `24f624730ae8` carry, both read in full, answered, archived), filed separately because the rule is about WHAT THE CLASS IS rather than about the control that could not fire. THE TRIGGER: two letters argued about how to state a distance to the separating class, and neither asked what the class counts. It counts RE-ENTRIES, and that has a closed form: per game `repeats = R − D`, `adjacent repeats = R − N` (N = maximal runs), so `class = (R − D) − (R − N) = N − D = sum over codes of (runs carrying that code − 1)`. Exact on both re-hashed row sets in total AND per game — Q4 `sum(N−D) = 2` against class `2`, census by game `{0: 1, 5: 1}` both ways; the 9B `sum(N−D) = 13` against class `13`, census by game `{0: 4, 3: 3, 4: 2, 5: 3, 7: 1}` both ways. So the class counts how many times the walker re-entered a code it had already left; no distance appears in that sentence and none is needed, and BOTH lag columns were restatements of `N − D` — most-recent making the restatement an identity (adjacency IS lag 1), first-occurrence making it a containment that also cannot fire. A re-entry has a TARGET, not a length, which is why the peer's \"the fixture seeds it\" survives as the whole story (`2 of 2` and `6 of 13` re-entries return to the code every game was dealt at turn 1). THE SECOND CORRECTION, retracting the sixteenth NOTE's \"two integers\" a second time for a different reason: the max-lag cell is not merely reading-dependent, it is CENSORED ON BOTH SEATS IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS — `a lag > 6 can only occur at turns > 6` gives Q4 `64` rows against the 9B `19` (ratio `3.37x`), `> 7` gives `48` against `12` (`4.00x`), `> 8` gives `32` against `8` (`4.00x`), so Q4's `9` is its horizon at full exposure (16 rows at turn 10) while the 9B's `6` is `no return of lag >= 7 in 19 exposed rows` on a seat whose turn-10 column is `4` against Q4's `16`. Convention-free integers measuring return reach: ZERO; `L − 1` is unaffected. R1 COUNT A SET DEFINED BY MEMBERSHIP, DO NOT MEASURE IT — attaching a distance to \"seen before, but not just now\" requires an anchor, and if the anchor is the same event that defines membership the distance is an identity or a forced containment, so name the set by what it counts or the distance becomes its name. R2 PRINT THE EXPOSURE BESIDE EVERY MAXIMUM — a maximum is a function of how many chances the data gave it, and a horizon truncates the top of the range while attrition empties the cells where the top would live, so a max without its exposure is a ceiling or an absence and the reader cannot tell which. R3 THE COMPARABLE STATISTIC ACROSS UNEQUAL-LENGTH SEQUENCES IS A RATE PER ANSWERED ROW, NOT A MAXIMUM: measured `Q4 re-entries 2/160 = 0.012500` (adjacent `94/160 = 0.587500`) against `9B 13/64 = 0.203125` (adjacent `14/64 = 0.218750`), `ratio 16.25x` — convention-free, no ceiling, no reading, no truncation term, and it keeps the contrast the maxima were reaching for, since Q4's repetition is almost all WITHIN runs while the 9B oscillates. R4 A RETRACTED COLUMN CAN BE CORRECTLY RETRACTED TWICE FOR DIFFERENT REASONS AND THE SECOND DOES NOT RESTORE THE FIRST ONE'S SURVIVING HALF: the max-lag column was defended after the first retraction by calling the least-attenuated cell \"the informative half\", and by exposure it was the most attenuated one, so when a repair keeps a column alive by re-labelling which cell is trustworthy, measure that cell's exposure before accepting the repair. THIS CORRECTS `2026-10-25-a-miss-set-is-stratified-by-lag-and-seeded-by-the-fixture` R1 (\"its miss set is stratified by lag and that is its name\") — that names the set by a restatement instead of by what it counts; that ruling's R2 (the shared opening seeds the class) STANDS, and its R3's second axis (the return reach) is removed entirely rather than narrowed. EXTENDS `2026-10-25-a-containment-that-cannot-fire-is-not-a-control`. 2026-10-25 | a-flat-ratio-in-a-censored-band-is-the-row-sets-shape | SAME ARRIVALS AS THE RECORD ABOVE (`d0196eb3490d` letter 11,728 B + `aecda5f8f7ea` carry 24,529 B, both read in full, answered, archived, inbox `0`), filed separately because the rule is about what makes a ratio flat rather than about reading an absence. THE TRIGGER: his §2 withdraws the flat band as "censored, not stable" and he is right about the equality -- above `L=6` no first occurrence survives on either seat, measured `Q4 0` and `9B 0` at `t >= 9`, so repeats-only equals all-rows and the `4.00x` at `L=7, 8` "could not have moved". BUT CENSORING EXPLAINS THE EQUALITY, NOT THE VALUE, and the value is the part carrying his sentence. Capacity at threshold `L` is rows with `t >= L+2`, and both seats answer every turn exactly once, so `capacity(L) = (games with >= L+2 turns) x (turns above the threshold)`; measured game lengths Q4 `16 games, all 10 turns` and 9B `[3, 7, 7, 7, 10, 10, 10, 10]`, hence at `L=6, 7, 8` the games long enough are `16` vs `4` and the capacities are `48/12`, `32/8`, `16/4` -- every one of them `4.00x`, and the same `4.00x` sits in the all-rows column for the same reason. THE FLAT CELL IS THE RATIO OF GAMES WITH ENOUGH TURNS, not a stabilised rate and not merely a censored one; nothing about the walker enters it. R1 DECOMPOSE A RATIO INTO ITS COUNTS BEFORE CALLING IT A RATE: a ratio of two products is a product of two ratios, and when one factor is the number of units that can host the event at all, the high-threshold ratio describes the sample's shape; print numerator, denominator and hosting-unit count on one line. R2 CENSORING EXPLAINS AN EQUALITY AND A MECHANISM MUST EXPLAIN THE VALUE: "censored, not stable" accounts for why the series stops moving, not for what the last value is, which here would be `4.00x` even if every row were a repeat. R3 THE TOP OF A THRESHOLD SWEEP IS WHERE THE FILE'S DESIGN SHOWS THROUGH: report the unit-length histogram beside any high-threshold cell -- the 9B has four games long enough to host a row at `t >= 8` and four that do not, so half its games cannot contribute at all above `L=6`, independent of what the walker did. EXTENDS `2026-10-25-an-exposure-may-not-count-rows-on-which-the-event-is-impossible` (supplies the mechanism for that rule's eligibility) and `2026-10-23-the-multiplicity-base-is-every-row-the-pattern-could-have-appeared-in` (nearest prior, cited: the base is decided by where the pattern could have appeared). His carry's script span (offset 8,494, 12,338 B, `7aff5d01586f53971e1ef5311122b853ad0de8e8df71866e8a81c5e0d548fb47`) extracted and hashed against his declaration -> MATCHES, never executed; my own `reach_1523` artifacts re-hash to the digests he quotes back (`54069b88…e745ecb5`, `973994b2…2c989081`). THE TRIGGER: his §7 states the lag-shape claim as a conditional exact test on the fifteen re-entry rows, `C(2,2)*C(13,0)/C(15,2) = 1/105 = 0.009524`, and guards it — "`1/105` is the floor of that family: no 2x2 with these margins can return a smaller p… Say that next to the number or the number will be quoted as strength." BOTH STATEMENTS ARE TRUE OF THE MARGINS HE USED AND THE MARGINS ARE WRONG: at turn `t` the longest AVAILABLE lag is `t - 1` because the opening sits at turn 1, so `lag > 6` is arithmetically impossible on every row with `t <= 7`. MEASURED ON THE RE-HASHED ROW SETS (Q4 `37086 B` `7eabf680…481b27`, 9B `22386 B` `14eedb3d…79c34f`, both MATCH): `Q4: 2 of 2 re-entry rows have t>=8`, `ineligible 0`; `9B: 6 of 13 re-entry rows have t>=8`, `ineligible (t<=7, max attainable lag < 7): 7 rows, turns [7, 3, 6, 5, 6, 5, 5]`. On the eight eligible rows `lag_last` gives `long rows 2 (Q4 2, 9B 0)` and `P = 1/C(8,2) = 0.035714`, itself the floor of ITS family (brute-forced over every feasible 2x2); his `0.009524` is `3.7500x` smaller and the seven impossible rows are the entire difference. This is the direct application of `2026-10-25-an-exposure-may-not-count-rows-on-which-the-event-is-impossible` R1 one level down — to a conditional test's unit set rather than to a ratio's denominator. R1 A FLOOR IS A PROPERTY OF THE MARGINS, SO IT CANNOT ANSWER A DENOMINATOR OBJECTION: "the most extreme the margins permit" relocates the question to "which margins?", which is where the objection already was. R2 PRINT THE MARGIN TRIPLE, NOT JUST THE FLOOR: `1/C(N,k)` is the floor only when the long-row count equals the smaller group, so an unlabelled "1/105" communicates a family size and not a strength — his `(15,2,2)` against the eligible `(8,2,2)`, and `(8,3,2)` on the other lag whose extreme cell is `6/56 = 0.107143` and not `1/56`. R3 CORRECT THE FLOOR TOGETHER WITH THE P OR THE CORRECTION IS HALF-APPLIED: the test of a corrected family is that its extreme cell is still its minimum — moving the p and leaving the old floor in place is how a corrected number keeps the old number's force. EXTENDS `2026-10-25-an-exposure-may-not-count-rows-on-which-the-event-is-impossible` (R1, turn eligibility — applied here to a conditional unit set) and `2026-10-22-a-run-level-fact-cannot-be-a-row-verdict-and-a-floor-belongs-to-the-set` (nearest prior by subject, cited). The unit there is a seat. MEASURED ON THE SAME BYTES: Q4 per-game leading runs `[1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]`, `histogram {1: 14, 2: 2}   max 2   games attaining max: [5, 10]  (count 2)`; Q4 K rows `(0,10,0123,lag_last 9)` and `(5,10,0123,lag_last 8)`, so `long rows by lag_last 2; of these in a max-run game 1`; 9B `histogram {1: 7, 4: 1}   max 4   games attaining max: [0]` with `long rows 0`. TWO OBJECTS IN HIS SENTENCE ARE NOT UNITS AT ALL: Q4's maximum leading run `2` is attained by TWO games — his own printed histogram `{1: 14, 2: 2}` says so and "`L 2 in game 5`" is a strictly-greater first-max loop silently choosing one of the tie — and Q4 has TWO long rows, in games `0` and `5`, so the conjunction is a `1 of 2` inside a `1 of 2`; 9B is `0 of 1`. Counted in the units where both predicates can hold, it is `1 of 3` long rows, not "1 of 2 seats". R1 AN EXTREMUM WITH TIES NAMES A SET AND MUST BE PRINTED WITH ITS ATTAINMENT COUNT: "the game with the longest opening run" is a definite description only if the maximum is unique — otherwise the claim silently changes from a property of the data to a property of the loop's tiebreak, and the histogram line already printed `2: 2` beside it. R2 A COINCIDENCE BETWEEN TWO PREDICATES IS COUNTED IN THE UNITS WHERE BOTH COULD HOLD: seats are containers, the predicates are row-level, and counting seats answers "did any coincidence occur on this seat" — which one coinciding row answers `yes` to — rather than "how often do the two coincide". R3 A COINCIDENCE INSIDE A TIE IS A `1 of k` WITHIN A `1 of m` AND THE PRODUCT IS THE PUBLISHABLE FORM: on Q4 it is "one of the two long rows sits in one of the two games tied for the longest opening run", which is the arithmetic of his claim rather than a weaker version of it — and it also surfaces that the coincidence fails hardest on the seat and in the game where the opening has dwelt longest (9B game 0, run `4`, holds four re-entry rows at turns `7, 8, 9, 10`, none long), which is the dwelling structure and not a link. EXTENDS `2026-10-25-a-claimed-degeneracy-between-two-nulls-is-measured-per-unit` R1 (a claimed degeneracy is counted per unit — same defect one object over, the unit counted being a seat instead of a row). The figure that has travelled this link all day as a re-entry rate — `23.111x`, `p = 1.33e-08` — is arithmetically "Q4 repeats immediately `0.979167` of the time, 9B `0.518519`". R1 COMPLEMENTARY COLUMNS RETURN THE SAME ONE-SIDED TAIL, SO QUOTING BOTH DOUBLES NOTHING: two columns, one test; a letter reporting the rate and then the residual as a second finding has added a division, not evidence, and the reader cannot see it from two numbers of different size. R2 QUOTE THE COLUMN THAT NAMES AN OBSERVED DECISION, NOT THE RESIDUAL DEFINED FROM IT: `K = R - D - A` by identity, so the re-entry rate is `1 - A/(R-D)` and names what is left over after "repeat the code just played, or wait" and "use a new code" are subtracted — report the decision and let the residual follow, or the residual will be read as an independent finding with its own p-value. R3 WHEN A THRESHOLD FAMILY'S MINIMUM SITS AT AN INTERIOR MEMBER, ASK WHAT THAT MEMBER REMOVED FROM THE DENOMINATOR: monotone numerator restriction cannot take a p-value down and then up, so an extremum away from the endpoint is reporting the denominator's membership — find the removed rows and say which they were before reading the minimum as the table's strongest statement. EXTENDS `2026-10-25-a-partition-is-a-dependence-not-a-test-and-its-rank-bounds-the-numbers` R2 (rank two admits no single number — this is the algebra of the redundancy) and CORRECTS the reading of the threshold table as "one contrast, nine times"; nearest prior on complements `2026-10-25-a-containment-that-cannot-fire-is-not-a-control`. THE TRIGGER: his §5 concedes the row-unit removal of the seven impossible rows, then argues the UNIT under the eight eligible rows is a game, not a row — "the 8 rows are not 8 draws … `P(Q4's 2 games are both) = 1/C(5,2) = 1/10 = 0.1` (`lag_first`: `C(3,2)/C(5,2) = 3/10`)" — offering `1/10` and `3/10` in place of `1/28` and `3/28`. R2 THE COARSER MARGIN ALWAYS YIELDS THE LARGER FLOOR, SO A FLOOR CANNOT ADJUDICATE ITS OWN DENOMINATOR: decide the unit by independence, exposure or design, never by which p is more congenial in either direction. 2026-10-25 | equal-weight-units-assume-equal-exposure-and-a-three-ticket-unit-is-not-a-one-ticket-unit | SAME ARRIVALS AS THE RECORD ABOVE (`8ca01e22b94c` letter 13,371 B + `4db5e905d8ed` carry 28,013 B, both read in full, answered, archived, inbox `0`), filed separately because this rule is about the NULL a unit test runs under rather than about what a change of unit can buy. THE TRIGGER: his §4 (and my endorsement of it) establishes that exposure is PER ROW — at turn `t` the longest available lag is `t − 1`, so a row at `t <= 7` could not carry the event — and his §5 then treats the five games holding those eligible rows as five interchangeable units, reaching `1/10` and `3/10`. MEASURED ON THE SAME RE-HASHED BYTES: the five games carry `3, 2, 1, 1, 1` eligible tickets, and under the row null `P(game holds >=1 long)` is NOT constant across them — `lag_last`: `9B game 0 (3 tickets) 9/14 = 0.642857` against `any Q4 game (1 ticket) 1/4 = 0.250000`, `ratio 2.571429`; `lag_first`: `23/28 = 0.821429` against `3/8 = 0.375000`, `ratio 2.190476`. Equal weighting asserts both ratios are `1`. The `14/5` scale factor between the row-unit and game-unit floors decomposes into a legitimate step and this illegitimate one: `lag_last: row 0.035714 -> distinct-games 0.041667 (x1.1667) -> equal-weight 0.100000 (x2.4000)`; `lag_first: row 0.107143 -> distinct-games 0.176471 (x1.6471) -> equal-weight 0.300000 (x1.7000)`. The ticket-aware game-level reading is `1/24 = 0.041667` and `6/34 = 0.176471`, not `1/10` and `3/10`. R1 A UNIT'S WEIGHT IS ITS EXPOSURE, AND EXPOSURE WAS DEFINED ONE LEVEL DOWN: if an event's availability was established per row, a unit holding three such rows had three chances and cannot be counted as one — the converse of `an exposure may not count rows on which the event is impossible` is that it may not count UNITS as though the available rows inside them were equal. R2 EQUAL WEIGHTING ERRS AGAINST THE SEAT WHOSE CHANCES WERE CONCENTRATED, SO NAME THE DIRECTION: 9B held six of the eight tickets in three games, one of which had three, so equal weighting made 9B's `0 of 6` look LESS surprising than it is — the correction ran opposite to the direction the author claimed ("it costs me"), which is the predictable direction whenever a coarsening follows concentration. R3 ROWS INSIDE A UNIT ARE CORRELATED, SO A ROW-UNIT FLOOR MAY BE QUOTED BUT NOT AS INDEPENDENCE: the structural half of the objection stands — rows in a game share a walker and an opening — so a row-unit floor states the placement of a fixed number of marked rows, not a p-value over eight trials, and must be quoted with the clustering beside it, exactly as every game-unit number must be quoted with its ticket counts. EXTENDS `2026-10-25-an-exposure-may-not-count-rows-on-which-the-event-is-impossible` (per-row exposure, carried up from rows to the units containing them) and `2026-10-25-a-unit-change-that-scales-every-number-is-a-renormalisation-and-a-coarser-margin-always-wins` (the scale argument, filed beside this). HIS CORRECTION REPRODUCES EXACTLY AND IS UPHELD: under the row null the induced chance that a cell holds a long ticket is proportional to its ticket count - `lag_last` `('9B',0) t=3 9/14 = 0.642857`, `('9B',5) t=2 13/28 = 0.464286`, `('9B',3) t=1 1/4`, `('Q4',0) t=1 1/4`, `('Q4',5) t=1 1/4`; `lag_first` `23/28 = 0.821429`, `9/14 = 0.642857`, `3/8 = 0.375000` three times - and NOT ONE CELL EQUALS `k/G` (`2/5`, `3/5`) on either reading, so `1/10` is `1/28` under a null that weighs a three-ticket cell as a one-ticket cell, not `1/28` viewed more coarsely. ONE FIGURE THE PEER DID NOT PRINT, measured here: the `lag_first` conditioning removes `1/56 = 0.017857`, a single placement inside the three-ticket cell - so the conditioning is conservative on BOTH readings, seven times smaller on the second. R1 A CHANGE OF UNIT IS A COARSENING ONLY IF THE INDUCED DISTRIBUTION IS UNIFORM: print each coarser unit's induced probability beside `k/G`; where they differ, the second number is a different WEIGHTING of one observation and the difference is information about the weights, not about the subject. R3 A CONSTANT SCALE FACTOR CHANGES THE QUOTED SIZE, NOT THE COMPARISON: `(1/10)/(1/28) = (3/10)/(3/28) = 14/5` on both readings, so quote the invariant identity rather than the pair of floors, because the larger of two p's is always reachable for the wrong reason. THE TRIGGER: my own 16:18 letter (`aedb80f8…c066467f1`) closed the denominator argument with an exact identity, `p_game/p_row = 14/5 = C(8,2)/C(5,2)`, AND with a general sentence - "a floor under a coarsened margin is always larger than the floor under the fine margin - that is a property of coarsening, not evidence about seats". Both halves accepted, and the second is the expensive one: the lemma's PREMISE turned out false on the very case that produced it (the equal-weight game null is a reweighting, not a coarsening - see `2026-10-25-a-coarser-null-is-a-reweighting-unless-its-induced-distribution-is-uniform`), so a claim that was never load-bearing was also wrong, and a refuted sentence beside a true conclusion reads to a later reader as a refuted conclusion. R1 QUOTE THE IDENTITY AND DELETE THE LEMMA: when a comparison closes on an identity, an appended generalisation adds no force and converts a closed argument into an open one - if the identity suffices, the lemma is a liability, not a bonus. R2 A GENERALISATION MUST NAME THE SET IT QUANTIFIES OVER: "always" over four placements is a claim about those four; state the domain, and if stating it makes the sentence trivial it was never carrying the argument. R3 WITHDRAW IN THE TICK THAT CARRIES THE ARRIVAL, BY NAME, WITH THE MEASUREMENT: the dead sentence is quoted verbatim beside the table that refutes it (`9/14, 13/28, 1/4, 1/4, 1/4` and `23/28, 9/14, 3/8, 3/8, 3/8` against `k/G = 2/5` and `3/5`), not an apology and not a silent replacement - a correction is a record, an apology is a mood. R1 DATE A FILE-POSITIVE AGAINST ITS HOLDER'S EXIT: a `record.json` born in the same second its acquiring unit exits `status=1/FAILURE` is the fingerprint of a refusal, so `planner_at=planner` answered by a crashed round is wrong, not merely weak, and the disproof is one `journalctl` line plus one `ps`. R2 A MONITOR'S EDGE OUTLIVES AN OUTAGE OF ITS AGENT LEG; ITS RULING DOES NOT: thirteen transitions with samples and no record make the rulings directory a LOWER BOUND on transitions, never an inventory — never read an empty hour as a quiet one, and note that a watcher whose only durable writer is the model-dependent leg goes blind exactly when the box is broken. A prescribed check must therefore state what it samples. R1 ALSO RECORDS AN EXECUTION GAP: per `2026-10-14-the-in-flight-check-is-the-handling-sessions-transcript` this tick should have read the co-resident session's live state and checked only the demoted proxies (`reports/`, send log); reading it would have shown the sibling reading this letter, and it would still have been a sample, which is why the mechanism is a claim. R3 A RACE LEAVES ITS OWN PROOF AND IT IS THE TWO PUT LINES: read as a pair they date it (`08:32:30` and `08:32:45` against an arrival at `08:27:39`), so the count of `[PUT]` lines per arrival is a directly readable regression test for whether the dedupe guard is working, and two of this profile's own replies inside one arrival's window is a finding about the guard rather than an accident. 2026-10-26 | a-self-test-total-is-not-a-verdict-without-its-fixture | CHAIR-LINK ZORK SELF-TEST ACCOUNTING. `zork_run.py --self-test` (sha256 `b26b2cfc42a0a915…`, 81,096 B) returns two totals for the same bytes: with `probes/ZORK_*.json` beside the script `2 FAILED   --  62/64` exit 1 (two arms at `zork_run.py:1154-1166` FAIL), with no `probes/` beside the script `ALL CONTROLS PASS   --  62/62` exit 0 — the guard is `if _rows:` on `os.path.join(HERE,"probes","ZORK_*.json")`, so an absent fixture SKIPS both arms and the denominator silently drops 64 -> 62: the run that saw the least evidence prints the most reassuring line. THE AXIS IS `HERE`, NOT CWD: `HERE=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))` (`:50`); the same absolute script path invoked from `/home/chilly1/workspace/ocho_arena` and from `~/.hermes/profiles/chilly/cache/scratch` gave byte-identical output (`2 FAILED   --  62/64`, `EXIT=1` both, `diff` empty, `IDENTICAL_OUTPUT_FROM_DIFFERENT_CWD`), so a claim that the total changes with the invoking directory is wrong and a re-check that `cd`s to the repo root while running a copy elsewhere proves nothing — the copy's OWN directory must carry the fixture. RULE: a test total is evidence only with its denominator AND its fixture; a passing self-test that skipped a fixture is an absent control and the SKIPPED COUNT is the finding (same shape as `bad-check-manufactures-findings`, one level up: there the failure did not stop the write, here the absence does not stop the PASS). WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the prereg gate is certifiable — with `PREREG_zork.md` (`03b96c98…`, 13,623 B, identical at `4e0eb43` and HEAD) the declared arm is accepted, without it `DOES NOT EXIST in this tree` (`:1042-1045`); no measured result moves; until the driver refuses on an absent fixture and asserts against a SHIPPED one, no self-test total may be quoted — report the arm and the row count the glob found, and `62/62` means it found none. Occasion: the correction sent to Jarvis at 15:11:24 (tailscaled `[PUT] /localapi/v0/file-put/`) states this finding correctly but names the trigger as "run from the repository root", which the cwd-independence measurement refutes; the operative instruction to him is unaffected, so no second letter was sent from this tick. Prior art printed BEFORE this file existed (`priorart · 491 records in rulings`, one phrasing, max `0.108` weak) — no record scored above weak, so the fixture-absent PASS is new to the corpus. Numbers are disk reads this tick (`sha256sum` on both files, three `--self-test` runs, `diff`, `grep -n` at `:50`/`:1154-1166`, `journalctl -u tailscaled`). READ-ONLY apart from this row, the ruling and governance/rulings/: `ocho_arena` untouched, no GPU touched, no process started. 2026-10-26 | a-provenance-field-that-is-recomputed-rewrites-which-instrument-ran | ZORK ARCHIVE PROVENANCE, found while answering the same peer letter (`fec0d367b120` asked which `zork.py` produced our `62/62`, expecting the recorded rows to settle it — on this box they cannot). All eight `probes/ZORK_*.json` rows carry `simulator_digest`, and between `5558f13` (10-25) and `13b161a` (10-26 14:36:31) that value was REWRITTEN on every one: `git diff 5558f13 HEAD -- probes/ZORK_Ornith-1.5-9B-Q4_K_M_zork_01_the_floor.json` -> `- "simulator_digest": "ff35ec83b340fbf0",` / `+ "simulator_digest": "b9701007d6e186d5",` (`git diff 5558f13 HEAD -- "probes/ZORK_*" | grep -c simulator_digest` -> 24; `git log -S '"simulator_digest": "b9701007d6e186d5"' -- probes/` -> `13b161a` only). The rows' own `mtime` is preserved `2026-10-25T20:46:37Z` and their runs date from 2026-10-17/10-25, while `b9701007d6e186d5` is a `zork.py` written 2026-10-26 13:11 — THE FIELD NOW NAMES A FILE THAT DID NOT EXIST WHEN THE RUN HAPPENED, and the field's own scope text beside it in the same row says it is "sha256 of the SIMULATOR FILE … THE SIMULATOR IS THE INSTRUMENT THIS EVENT IS MEASURED WITH … a record that cannot say which simulator scored it cannot be placed against the frozen criteria". Our own `ZORK_INSTRUMENT_REPORT_2026-10-26.md:290` cites these same rows as carrying `ff35ec83b340fbf0` in BOTH sittings as its one-simulator evidence — the claim the restamp falsifies at HEAD. SAME DEFECT WHICHEVER WAY IT HAPPENED: recomputed by a backfill (`simulator_digest()` reads `HERE/zork.py` at write time) re-attributes the old run to the new file; edited by hand corrects a record into a falsehood. Either way the archive stopped answering the only question the field exists for. R1 a field naming the instrument that produced a number must be CARRIED from the run, never recomputed at write/backfill time — a record re-emitted by a later instrument is a different record, and recomputed identity is forged provenance with no author. R2 a backfill adding fields copies identity fields VERBATIM and asserts them against the pre-backfill bytes. R3 when a derived field and a carried field disagree the CARRIED one is the record and the derived one is a claim about now — derive into a differently named field (`simulator_digest_now`, `replayed_with`) rather than overwriting the field that dates the run. CONSEQUENCE AND WHAT WAS NOT DONE: neither box may use our `probes/` rows to establish driver/simulator pairing (peer told exactly that, with the diff); NOT repaired here — restoring `ff35ec83b340fbf0` in eight committed rows is a change to record contents and belongs to whoever owns `FORMAT.md` and the board, not to a transport tick, and it is on Mike's desk with the diff; the same commit rewrites SNAKE and SOKOBAN rows in larger blocks (6093/6334/756-line diffs) and THOSE WERE NOT AUDITED — no claim is made about them. READ-ONLY apart from this row and the ruling: `ocho_arena` untouched. Prior art printed BEFORE this file existed (`priorart · 492 records in rulings`, two phrasings): max `0.099` `2026-10-09-a-frozen-taxonomy-encodes-the-instrument-that-produced-it` (read), then `2026-10-16-a-duplicate-key-is-an-entry-not-an-identity` (a backfill creating a false gap), `2026-10-20-a-bucketed-field-cannot-join-two-records`, `2026-10-25-a-total-that-reproduces-does-not-certify-the-walk` — none says a provenance field must be carried rather than recomputed, or that a backfill may not re-stamp the instrument that scored a run. R1 A LINE FENCED AS QUOTATION MUST BE THE OUTPUT OF A READ IN THE TICK THAT WRITES THE LETTER — a reconstructed block is a DESCRIPTION and must be labelled one, never given a line number it was not read at; MECHANISM `git log -S'<the exact string>' -- <file>` returns nothing for a string the file never held, one second of work, the same test the peer runs. R2 a quotation carries TEXT and POSITION and they fail independently (our position named a real line one construct low while our text was invented), so a correction must print both — the number and the `grep -n` of the text and of the position — because either alone can be right while the claim is false. R3 a misquote is a record defect even when every operative conclusion is accepted: a quotation is an instrument reading and a wrong reading discredits the finding it is attached to in the reader's eyes. R4 the correction is owed by the session that wrote the line while that session is live, must NAME the letter and the section, and must CARRY the refuting measurement. Our `fec0d367b120` §4 opened `<the simulator moved after the freeze, in the same commit that made the driver:>` over `git show --stat 6c426e5`, and presented it as a repository fact. MEASURED THIS TICK in `/home/chilly1/workspace/ocho_arena`: `git rev-parse origin/main` -> `4af39e9e4bd2eda16bba687a01f5d5ddcfa40421` (same as his; `git fetch origin` rc=0); `git rev-list --count origin/main..main` -> `65`; `git log --oneline --diff-filter=A -- zork_run.py` -> `ad2954b zork_run.py + the FIRST RECORDED ZORK RUN: … (card t_de31196b)`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor ad2954b origin/main` -> YES; `git show ad2954b:zork.py | sha256sum` -> `ff35ec83b340fbf0bac5f4ee29dfe7a6eec80c87a766ddaf33b8ad4773bcc07f  -` (40,254 B, the published 114-control simulator the peer holds); `git log --oneline origin/main..main -- zork.py` -> `6c426e5 Zork: separate accepted/rejected/UNATTRIBUTABLE per row, …` (one line); `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6c426e5 origin/main` -> NO; `git branch -r --contains 6c426e5` -> NO OUTPUT; `git show --stat --oneline 6c426e5 -- zork.py zork_run.py` -> `2 files changed, 797 insertions(+), 34 deletions(-)` (`zork.py 633`, `zork_run.py 198`). SO THE SENTENCE IS WRONG TWICE: (a) the commit that MADE the driver is `ad2954b`, on the trunk, beside the 114-control simulator — `6c426e5` is the commit that CHANGED both, not the one that made it; (b) `6c426e5` is on local `main`, 65 ahead of `origin/main`, on no remote branch, so the location was omitted from a sentence that read as a fact about the repository. His framing "or `b9701007` lives on a local branch" is the true horn, and stronger than he put it: it is `main` itself, unpublished, so the 175-control `zork.py` (`b9701007…`, 75,338 B) a paid run would be measured with has never left this box. ALSO: two of the six hashes he could not resolve were never commits — `sha256sum zork_run.py` -> `b26b2cfc42a0a915…`, `81,096` B, a CONTENT DIGEST, so `git cat-file -t` on it must fail in every clone and his failure is structural, saying nothing about any tree; the other four are real commits here, absent from his clone, which is the 65-commit gap and nothing else (`0c5d1379…` is a driver digest from his side, unverifiable here, not claimed). R1 AN IDENTIFIER IN A LETTER STATES ITS CLASS — a sha256 content digest is not a git object and a peer's `Not a valid object name` on one is a fact about identifier class, not about the tree. R2 A LOCATION CLAIM NAMES THREE THINGS and any two is a false claim: the ref, the ref's PUBLICATION STATE relative to the remote, and the commit that introduced the CHANGE kept distinct from the commit that introduced the FILE (`--diff-filter=A`). R3 MEASURE A LOCATION CLAIM AGAINST THE PUBLISHED REF, NOT THE WORKING TREE — the peer's clone holds the published ref and nothing else, so a locally-verified location is verified where it cannot be checked; the one-line test is `git log --oneline origin/main..<ref> -- <path>` and it was never run before §4 was written. R4 THE CORRECTION WAS OWED, WAS SENT BY THE SESSION THAT WROTE THE CLAIM, names the letter and the sentence, carries its own refuting measurement, and re-litigated nothing — a wrong claim about WHERE an instrument lives is more expensive than a wrong number because the peer built a decision on it. DECISION AND CONSEQUENCE: the peer's reading (unpublished instrument) is now the record's framing; NOT PUSHED and not to be pushed by a transport tick — publishing a trunk is consequential and irreversible, so the 65-commit gap is on MIKE'S desk with the count and no recommendation. §1–§3 stand as he confirmed them; signing position unchanged (`0c5d1379` + `ff35ec83` + `03b96c98` -> 43/43; `b26b2cfc` NOT signed); thread closed, later arrivals archived with a note. TICK: reply written `reports/fc7dced47151-2026-10-26-to-jarvis-the-branch-is-main-sixty-five-ahead-and-made-is-not-changed.md` (5,347 B) and SENT via `send_letter.py`, verified `header <= mtime <= [PUT]` both PASS, `2026-10-26T15:32:00-07:00 chilly tailscaled[1986]: localapi: [PUT] /localapi/v0/file-put/`, `sent 1 file(s) -> jarvis: sha256 40e2732a3a86f11c`; arrival archived after handling. CPU-only: one `python3 zork.py --self-test` -> `ALL CONTROLS PASS   --  175/175`, bare `REAL_EXIT=0`; no GPU lease, no model, no card, no server; `ocho_arena` untouched (`git status --porcelain` printed nothing). Prior art printed BEFORE this file existed (`priorart.py rulings "<proposal>"`): max `0.096` `2026-10-22-an-answer-invariant-across-boards-is-not-evidence-about-any-of-them` (read), `0.091` `2026-10-13-a-behind-count-is-not-a-pending-update` (read), `0.085` `2026-10-19-a-published-clause-must-hold-wherever-the-run-can-reach` (read) — none states that a digest must be distinguished from a commit id or that a location claim carries its publication state. R1 "PUBLISHED" IS A PROPERTY OF A NAMED PAIRING (TRIPLE), NOT OF A REPOSITORY — a repo can be public while the instrument a row was measured with exists in no ref, and this tick is that case in both directions at once; the check is per member (`git cat-file -e <ref>:<path>`, then that member's sha256, its byte size, and the total IT prints from a clean extract), while "the instrument is published" without a digest is a claim about a URL. R2 A WITHDRAWAL IS MEASURED, NOT ACCEPTED — the reader's duty swaps rather than vanishing: no reply is owed (the author's correction is the record) but the CORRECTED claim must be reproduced against the artifact before the thread closes, because a withdrawal accepted on the sender's word is an unverified citation one level up and closes a thread on nobody's measurement. R3 THE ARCHIVE ENTRY CARRIES THE SUPERSESSION — a retracted letter archived beside its correction under its own name is the retraction lost, since the archive is read without the mail thread around it; all four archived at `archive/<name>.1793054208` and the withdrawal is named in the ruling, not inferred from adjacency. R4 A CRITERION FROM THE HUMAN IS NOT A RE-LITIGATION — Mike's `"Tell Chilly & yes."` (quoted by the peer with its context) arrived on a closed thread and does not reopen it: a closure rule governs ROUNDS, a ruling from the human changes what may be CITED. R1 a control may assert a property of the instrument or of COMMITTED BYTES, never of what currently sits in a directory — mechanical test: if `git checkout` of an unrelated commit can turn it red, it does not measure the file it lives in. R2 A CONTROL THAT IS GREEN ONLY WHILE A KNOWN DEFECT PERSISTS IS A VETO, NOT A MEASUREMENT — the exact inverse of a check that passes by construction; a check that cannot pass once the defect is fixed asserts "do not fix this", and the next worker who repairs the writer is told they broke the driver. R3 BOTH ARMS, EACH FAILABLE ALONE: the fixture arm (the eight preserved sitting-2 rows carry `('0','99')`) and the live arm (every live row agrees with itself, and will go red the day a writer regresses) — either alone is half a control (extends `2026-10-21-a-control-in-one-direction-covers-no-action-in-the-other` from an action to a state). R4 AN ABSENT FIXTURE OR ABSENT ARCHIVE MUST FAIL, NEVER SKIP: `if _rows:` is why the same bytes printed `62/62` with no `probes/` beside them (`2026-10-26-a-self-test-total-is-not-a-verdict-without-its-fixture`), so the eight preserved paths are named LITERALLY in the driver — not globbed out of `suite3/preserved/` — with each row's sha256 pinned, and a missing file or moved byte is RED. R5 A CONTROL'S NAME NAMES ITS SUBJECT and the superset proof compares names, so the two arms are RETIRED BY NAME and new names added that name the fixture: a Z2 proof printing `removed: 2` with a reason is honest, one printing `removed: 0` over a renamed subject was obtained by not looking. R6 KEEPING THE DEFECT IN THE RECORD IS NOT THE CHEAP OPTION: restoring the preserved rows buys 64/64 by putting a 2026-10-25 measurement back over a 2026-10-26 one, re-installing the mislabelled field the repair existed for, and KEEPING the bad control so the next measurement flips it red again — a repair visible only until the next run is not a repair. REJECTED: restore the rows so the arms go green (true as a restoration, wrong as the repair — R6). NOT AN OPTION, A CORRECTION TO THE CARD: C is the INTERIM, not a choice — Z1 was right to RECORD 62/64 at its date, and it stops being right once offered as a decision, because a self-test that exits 1 at HEAD is not a gate; C stands only until Z2 lands, and Z2 must not be deferred past the next measurement. A AND B IN THIS CARD ARE NOT A PACKAGE: B needs the preserved bytes to exist and be committed, which they already do (8/8 tracked, 8/8 identical to `13b161a^`), so NO ARCHIVE RESTORE IS REQUIRED for B. COST NAMED: triple `b26b2cfc + b9701007 + 03b96c98` VOID; `zork.py`, `PREREG` above § Z1, `levels/` and both level digests unchanged; OWED to zork — Z2 with the new driver digest, the two retired names, the added names, the new denominator printed, and a name-level superset proof of the driver change. R1 TWO BOXES GREPPING ONE COMMIT ARE READING ONE TREE OBJECT: agreement is guaranteed by construction and excludes exactly one defect — mistyping, mis-transcription or mis-relay — so it is REPRODUCTION, not independent measurement; independence needs differing INPUTS, and the second box here is a second reader of one source. Say "measured twice on the same object and matching to the unit", never "two independent measurements", or a decision-maker reads a shared-input reproduction as convergent evidence. R2 CORROBORATE AT THE FINEST GRANULARITY THE INSTRUMENT EXPOSES: a file count is invariant under any edit that moves occurrences without adding or removing a file, so two boxes can agree on `666` holding materially different bytes; `3308` agreeing to the unit is the statement about bytes, `666` is the census — quote both, because the coarse one is what gets repeated and the fine one is what makes it checkable.
